tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", do neither.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

You are an independent research analyst. Your job is to build, **from scratch and blind**, the best list you can of a company's current leadership. Your list is the answer key used to find people the automated pipeline missed. You deliberately have no access to the repo's code or data. Don't ask for it, and don't try to infer it.

## Scope

- **Leadership** means: C-level (CEO, CTO, CFO, COO, CMO, CPO, CISO, CLO/General Counsel, CHRO/CPO-People, etc.), all VP levels (VP, SVP, EVP), Heads of departments, and founders still in an operating role.
- **Excluded:** board-only members, advisors, investors, former employees, and managers below Head level.

## Hard rules

- **No LinkedIn.** Don't fetch linkedin.com, and ignore LinkedIn search results entirely. The project excludes it as a source, so your answer key must play by the same rules or the comparison is unfair.
- Don't fetch sites whose ToS forbids automated access. Respect obvious paywalls.
- **Every person needs a URL** that you actually fetched and read, showing their name and title. A search snippet alone isn't enough. Search snippets can be stale or wrong.
- Prefer current information. Note the publication date of each source. Mark anything older than 18 months as `possibly stale`.
- Budget: about 25 searches and about 30 fetches per company. Stop when new searches stop turning up new people.

## Search strategy (in order)

1. The company's own site: `/about`, `/team`, `/leadership`, `/company`, the newsroom or press pages.
2. For public companies: the SEC EDGAR latest 10-K "Information about our Executive Officers" and the DEF 14A proxy.
3. Press releases and news, such as `"<company>" appoints`, `"<company>" names * as`, `"<company>" "VP of"`, `"<company>" "Head of"`, and `"<company>" chief * officer`.
4. Conference speaker bios, podcasts, and the company's engineering blog author pages (good for VPs and Heads).
5. For each department (engineering, product, finance, marketing, sales, operations, legal, people, security, design, data), do one targeted search if you haven't found its head yet.

Good evening! I'm doing well, thanks. Happy to build this with you. Here's Phase 0. I haven't written any code yet.

## What's already here
- 4 project subagents in `.claude/agents/`, plus `docs/initial-prompt.md`, `.gitattributes` (`eol=lf`) and `.gitignore` (which already excludes `.env`). There's also a `.claude/settings.json` that stops me reading `.env`.
- **Missing pieces:** `uv` isn't installed, and the only Python is 3.14 (via `py`). uv can download 3.12 itself once it's installed.

## Plan (one commit per phase, each ending with real output, a `phase-reviewer` run, and a stop for your review)

1. **Storage.** `schema.sql` (Postgres-compatible: no SQLite-only types, `CHECK` constraints instead of enums, ISO-8601 text timestamps), `db.py` (connect and init) and `repository.py` (parameterized queries only). I'll also set up the `pyproject.toml`/`uv` skeleton, Ruff and pytest, and write the first `DECISIONS.md` entries (LinkedIn ban, SQLite vs vector store).
2. **Sources and cache.** Shared fetcher with robots.txt check, about 1 request per second per host, a descriptive User-Agent and an on-disk cache keyed by URL hash. Three adapters, all with the same interface:
   - `company_site`: sitemap.xml, common paths and nav links, filtered by keywords like team/leadership/about/press.
   - `sec_edgar`: ticker → CIK, then the latest 10-K "Executive Officers" section and the DEF 14A.
   - `search`: targeted queries.
   If meetcampfire.com needs JavaScript to render, I'll stop and tell you.
3. **Extract, validate, resolve.**
   - Extract: chunk the pages, pre-filter with heuristics, then one tool-use call per chunk that returns Pydantic models.
   - Validate: drop anything whose evidence snippet doesn't literally appear in the source (after normalizing whitespace and case), and apply deterministic title rules.
   - Resolve: dedupe on normalized name, and settle conflicts by source priority then recency. Confidence is rule-based.
4. **Collect both companies.** Then run `coverage-scout` (blind) and `source-verifier`, diff the results, and generate `VALIDATION.md`. **Hard stop for your hand-check.**
5. **Chat agent.** The 3 typed tools, a tool-use loop with conversation history, and a system prompt that enforces the honesty rules.
6. **Eval and tests.** `eval/questions.yaml` (built from answers you've verified), `leadership eval`, and offline unit tests.
7. **UI.** Streamlit app with the sidebar, the Chat tab (streaming answers, Sources and Agent steps sections) and the Leadership tab, plus the theme and friendly error messages.
8. **Docs.** README, Mermaid diagram and screenshots, then `fresh-clone-tester` until it returns READY TO SUBMIT.

## Proposed changes to your schema

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data"
ENV_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".env"

DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"

load_dotenv(ENV_PATH, override=False, encoding="utf-8")

_WHERE_TO_GET = {
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "Get a key at https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys",
    "TAVILY_API_KEY": "Get a key at https://app.tavily.com (only needed for `leadership collect`)",
    "SEC_USER_AGENT": (
        'Set it to your name and contact email, e.g. "Jane Doe jane@example.com" '
        "(SEC policy: https://www.sec.gov/os/accessing-edgar-data). "
        "Only needed for `leadership collect`"
    ),
}


class MissingSettingError(RuntimeError):
    """A required environment variable is not set."""

    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        hint = _WHERE_TO_GET.get(name, "")
        super().__init__(
            f"Missing {name}. Add it to {ENV_PATH} (copy .env.example to .env). {hint}".strip()
        )


def get_setting(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the env var's value, or None if unset or blank."""
    value = os.getenv(name, "").strip()
    return value or None


def require_setting(name: str) -> str:
    value = get_setting(name)
    if value is None:
        raise MissingSettingError(name)
    return value


def llm_model() -> str:
    return get_setting("LLM_MODEL") or DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL


def company_dir(domain: str) -> Path:
    return DATA_DIR / domain


def db_path(domain: str) -> Path:
    return company_dir(domain) / "leadership.db"

-- Leadership store. Written to run unchanged on SQLite and PostgreSQL, apart from one
-- documented swap: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` auto-assigns ids in SQLite; in Postgres use
-- `id INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY`.
-- Conventions: booleans are INTEGER 0/1, timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC TEXT, enums are CHECKs.
--
-- `people`/`roles` hold the resolved current view. `facts` holds every claim with its evidence
-- (the audit trail). Nothing reaches `people`/`roles` without at least one backing fact.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS companies (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    domain      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    is_public   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_public IN (0, 1)),
    ticker      TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sources (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    url         TEXT    NOT NULL,
    source_type TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN ('company_site', 'sec_filing', 'search')),
    fetched_at  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    raw_path    TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- repo-relative path to the cached raw document
    UNIQUE (company_id, url)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS people (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

"""Shared vocabulary: enum values, source priority, name normalization, timestamps."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from datetime import UTC, datetime

FUNCTIONS = (
    "engineering",
    "product",
    "finance",
    "marketing",
    "sales",
    "operations",
    "legal",
    "people",
    "security",
    "design",
    "data",
    "other",
)
SENIORITIES = ("c_level", "vp", "head", "founder")
SOURCE_TYPES = ("company_site", "sec_filing", "search")
FACT_FIELDS = ("full_name", "title", "location", "bio")
CONFIDENCE_LEVELS = ("high", "medium", "low")

# Lower number wins a conflict. Derived from sources.source_type; never stored.
SOURCE_PRIORITY = {"company_site": 0, "sec_filing": 1, "search": 2}

_HONORIFICS = {"mr", "mrs", "ms", "dr", "prof", "jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv", "phd", "md", "mba"}


def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Dedupe key for a person's name.

    Strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics/suffixes, and single-letter middle initials:
    "Jason S. Warnick" and "jason warnick" map to the same key. Nicknames ("Vlad" vs
    "Vladimir") are deliberately not merged here.
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z\s'-]", " ", text).replace("'", "").replace("-", " ")
    tokens = [t for t in text.split() if t not in _HONORIFICS]
    if len(tokens) > 2:
        tokens = [tokens[0], *[t for t in tokens[1:-1] if len(t) > 1], tokens[-1]]
    return " ".join(tokens)


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()

"""Shared vocabulary: enum values, source priority, name normalization, timestamps."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from datetime import UTC, datetime

FUNCTIONS = (
    "engineering",
    "product",
    "finance",
    "marketing",
    "sales",
    "operations",
    "legal",
    "people",
    "security",
    "design",
    "data",
    "other",
)
SENIORITIES = ("c_level", "vp", "head", "founder")
SOURCE_TYPES = ("company_site", "sec_filing", "search")
FACT_FIELDS = ("full_name", "title", "location", "bio")
CONFIDENCE_LEVELS = ("high", "medium", "low")

# Lower number wins a conflict. Derived from sources.source_type; never stored.
SOURCE_PRIORITY = {"company_site": 0, "sec_filing": 1, "search": 2}

_HONORIFICS = {"mr", "mrs", "ms", "dr", "prof", "jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv", "phd", "md", "mba"}


def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Dedupe key for a person's name.

    Strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics/suffixes, and single-letter middle initials:
    "Jason S. Warnick" and "jason warnick" map to the same key. Nicknames ("Vlad" vs
    "Vladimir") are deliberately not merged here.
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z\s'-]", " ", text).replace("'", "").replace("-", " ")
    tokens = [t for t in text.split() if t not in _HONORIFICS]
    if len(tokens) > 2:
        tokens = [tokens[0], *[t for t in tokens[1:-1] if len(t) > 1], tokens[-1]]
    return " ".join(tokens)


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()

def connect(path: Path | str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open (creating if needed) a database with foreign keys on and the schema applied."""
    if str(path) != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return conn

"""All database reads and writes. Every query is parameterized.

Provenance invariants enforced here, not just in the pipeline:
- a fact needs a source and a non-blank evidence snippet;
- a person's location/bio and each role title can only be set if a matching fact exists.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from leadership.models import (
    CONFIDENCE_LEVELS,
    FACT_FIELDS,
    FUNCTIONS,
    SENIORITIES,
    SOURCE_TYPES,
    normalize_name,
    utc_now_iso,
)


class ProvenanceError(ValueError):
    """A write would store a claim without supporting evidence."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RoleIn:
    title_raw: str
    function: str
    seniority: str
    is_current: bool = True


_SENIORITY_ORDER = (
    "CASE r.seniority WHEN 'c_level' THEN 0 WHEN 'founder' THEN 1 WHEN 'vp' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END"
)


def _check_choice(name: str, value: str | None, allowed: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    if value is not None and value not in allowed:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid {name} {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(allowed)}")


class Repository:
    def __init__(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        self.conn = conn

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- companies / sources

    def upsert_company(
        self, name: str, domain: str, is_public: bool = False, ticker: str | None = None
    ) -> int:
        self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO companies (name, domain, is_public, ticker) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
               ON CONFLICT (domain) DO UPDATE SET
                 name = excluded.name, is_public = excluded.is_public, ticker = excluded.ticker""",
            (name, domain, int(is_public), ticker),
        )
        return self.conn.execute("SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain = ?", (domain,)).fetchone()[0]

    def get_company(self, domain: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM companies WHERE domain = ?", (domain,)).fetchone()
        return dict(row) if row else None

    def add_source(
        self, company_id: int, url: str, source_type: str, fetched_at: str, raw_path: str
    ) -> int:
        _check_choice("source_type", source_type, SOURCE_TYPES)
        self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO sources (company_id, url, source_type, fetched_at, raw_path)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
               ON CONFLICT (company_id, url) DO UPDATE SET
                 source_type = excluded.source_type,
                 fetched_at = excluded.fetched_at,
                 raw_path = excluded.raw_path""",
            (company_id, url, source_type, fetched_at, raw_path),
        )
        return self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM sources WHERE company_id = ? AND url = ?", (company_id, url)
        ).fetchone()[0]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- people / facts / roles

    def upsert_person(self, company_id: int, full_name: str, confidence: str = "low") -> int:
        """Get or create a person by normalized name. Does not overwrite resolved fields."""
        _check_choice("confidence", confidence, CONFIDENCE_LEVELS)
        key = normalize_name(full_name)
        if not key:
            raise ValueError(f"Name {full_name!r} normalizes to an empty string")
        self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO people (company_id, full_name, normalized_name, confidence, updated_at)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
               ON CONFLICT (company_id, normalized_name) DO NOTHING""",
            (company_id, full_name, key, confidence, utc_now_iso()),
        )
        return self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM people WHERE company_id = ? AND normalized_name = ?", (company_id, key)
        ).fetchone()[0]

    def add_fact(
        self,
        person_id: int,
        field: str,
        value: str,
        source_id: int,
        evidence_snippet: str,
        extracted_at: str | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        _check_choice("field", field, FACT_FIELDS)
        if not value or not value.strip():
            raise ProvenanceError(f"Fact {field!r} has an empty value")
        if not evidence_snippet or not evidence_snippet.strip():
            raise ProvenanceError(f"Fact {field}={value!r} has no evidence snippet")
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO facts (person_id, field, value, source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (person_id, field, value.strip(), source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at or utc_now_iso()),
        )
        return cur.lastrowid

    def _require_fact(self, person_id: int, field: str, value: str) -> None:
        row = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM facts WHERE person_id = ? AND field = ? AND value = ? LIMIT 1",
            (person_id, field, value),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ProvenanceError(f"No {field!r} fact with value {value!r} for person {person_id}")

    def update_person_resolved(
        self,
        person_id: int,
        *,
        full_name: str,
        confidence: str,
        location: str | None = None,
        bio: str | None = None,
        profile_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        _check_choice("confidence", confidence, CONFIDENCE_LEVELS)
        if location is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "location", location)
        if bio is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "bio", bio)
        self.conn.execute(
            """UPDATE people SET full_name = ?, location = ?, bio = ?, profile_url = ?,
                 confidence = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?""",
            (full_name, location, bio, profile_url, confidence, utc_now_iso(), person_id),
        )

    def replace_roles(self, person_id: int, roles: list[RoleIn]) -> None:
        for role in roles:
            _check_choice("function", role.function, FUNCTIONS)
            _check_choice("seniority", role.seniority, SENIORITIES)
            self._require_fact(person_id, "title", role.title_raw)
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM roles WHERE person_id = ?", (person_id,))
        self.conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO roles (person_id, title_raw, function, seniority, is_current)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [(person_id, r.title_raw, r.function, r.seniority, int(r.is_current)) for r in roles],
        )

    def clear_people(self, company_id: int) -> None:
        """Drop people (cascading to roles and facts) before a full re-resolve."""
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM people WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- collection runs

    def start_run(self, company_id: int) -> int:
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO collection_runs (company_id, started_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
            (company_id, utc_now_iso()),
        )
        return cur.lastrowid

    def finish_run(self, run_id: int, stats: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.conn.execute(
            "UPDATE collection_runs SET finished_at = ?, stats_json = ? WHERE id = ?",
            (utc_now_iso(), json.dumps(stats, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True), run_id),
        )

    def latest_run(self, domain: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT cr.* FROM collection_runs cr JOIN companies c ON c.id = cr.company_id
               WHERE c.domain = ? AND cr.finished_at IS NOT NULL
               ORDER BY cr.finished_at DESC, cr.id DESC LIMIT 1""",
            (domain,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        run = dict(row)
        run["stats"] = json.loads(run.pop("stats_json") or "{}")
        return run

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- reads for chat / UI

    def _roles_for(self, person_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        rows = self.conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT title_raw, function, seniority, is_current FROM roles r
                WHERE r.person_id = ? ORDER BY {_SENIORITY_ORDER}, r.title_raw""",
            (person_id,),
        ).fetchall()
        return [dict(r) | {"is_current": bool(r["is_current"])} for r in rows]

    def list_leaders(
        self, domain: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Current leaders with at least one current role matching the filters."""
        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
        rows = self.conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT p.id, p.full_name, p.location, p.confidence, p.profile_url,
                   (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.source_id) FROM facts f WHERE f.person_id = p.id)
                     AS source_count,
                   (SELECT MIN({_SENIORITY_ORDER}) FROM roles r
                     WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1) AS rank
                FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
                WHERE c.domain = ?
                  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM roles r WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1
                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?))
                ORDER BY rank, p.full_name""",
            (domain, function, function, seniority, seniority),
        ).fetchall()
        leaders = []
        for row in rows:
            person = dict(row)
            person.pop("rank")
            person["roles"] = [r for r in self._roles_for(person["id"]) if r["is_current"]]
            leaders.append(person)
        return leaders

    def count_leaders(
        self, domain: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
    ) -> int:
        """Distinct people (not roles) with a current role matching the filters."""
        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
        return self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM people p
               JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
               JOIN roles r ON r.person_id = p.id
               WHERE c.domain = ? AND r.is_current = 1
                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?)""",
            (domain, function, function, seniority, seniority),
        ).fetchone()[0]

    def get_person(self, domain: str, name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """People whose normalized name contains every token of `name`, with facts and sources.

        An exact normalized match wins outright; otherwise all token matches are returned so
        the caller can surface ambiguity instead of picking one.
        """
        query = normalize_name(name)
        if not query:
            return []
        candidates = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT p.* FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
               WHERE c.domain = ? ORDER BY p.full_name""",
            (domain,),
        ).fetchall()
        exact = [p for p in candidates if p["normalized_name"] == query]
        tokens = query.split()
        matches = exact or [
            p for p in candidates if all(t in p["normalized_name"].split() for t in tokens)
        ]
        return [self._person_detail(dict(p)) for p in matches]

    def _person_detail(self, person: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        facts = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT f.field, f.value, f.evidence_snippet, f.extracted_at,
                      s.id AS source_id, s.url, s.source_type, s.fetched_at
               FROM facts f JOIN sources s ON s.id = f.source_id
               WHERE f.person_id = ? ORDER BY f.field, s.source_type, s.url""",
            (person["id"],),
        ).fetchall()
        person.pop("normalized_name", None)
        person["roles"] = self._roles_for(person["id"])
        person["facts"] = [
            {
                "field": f["field"],
                "value": f["value"],
                "evidence_snippet": f["evidence_snippet"],
                "extracted_at": f["extracted_at"],
                "source": {
                    "url": f["url"],
                    "source_type": f["source_type"],
                    "fetched_at": f["fetched_at"],
                },
            }
            for f in facts
        ]
        person["source_count"] = len({f["source_id"] for f in facts})
        return person

"""Shared vocabulary: enum values, source priority, name normalization, timestamps."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from datetime import UTC, datetime

FUNCTIONS = (
    "engineering",
    "product",
    "finance",
    "marketing",
    "sales",
    "operations",
    "legal",
    "people",
    "security",
    "design",
    "data",
    "other",
)
SENIORITIES = ("c_level", "vp", "head", "founder")
SOURCE_TYPES = ("company_site", "sec_filing", "search")
FACT_FIELDS = ("full_name", "title", "location", "bio")
CONFIDENCE_LEVELS = ("high", "medium", "low")

# Lower number wins a conflict. Derived from sources.source_type; never stored.
SOURCE_PRIORITY = {"company_site": 0, "sec_filing": 1, "search": 2}

_HONORIFICS = {"mr", "mrs", "ms", "dr", "prof", "jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv", "phd", "md", "mba"}


def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Dedupe key for a person's name.

    Strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics/suffixes, and single-letter middle initials:
    "Jason S. Warnick" and "jason warnick" map to the same key. Nicknames ("Vlad" vs
    "Vladimir") are deliberately not merged here.
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z\s'-]", " ", text).replace("'", "").replace("-", " ")
    tokens = [t for t in text.split() if t not in _HONORIFICS]
    if len(tokens) > 2:
        tokens = [tokens[0], *[t for t in tokens[1:-1] if len(t) > 1], tokens[-1]]
    return " ".join(tokens)


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()

            raise ProvenanceError(f"No {field!r} fact with value {value!r} for person {person_id}")

    def update_person_resolved(
        self,
        person_id: int,
        *,
        full_name: str,
        confidence: str,
        location: str | None = None,
        bio: str | None = None,
        profile_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        _check_choice("confidence", confidence, CONFIDENCE_LEVELS)
        if location is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "location", location)
        if bio is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "bio", bio)
        self.conn.execute(
            """UPDATE people SET full_name = ?, location = ?, bio = ?, profile_url = ?,
                 confidence = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?""",
            (full_name, location, bio, profile_url, confidence, utc_now_iso(), person_id),
        )

    def replace_roles(self, person_id: int, roles: list[RoleIn]) -> None:
        for role in roles:
            _check_choice("function", role.function, FUNCTIONS)
            _check_choice("seniority", role.seniority, SENIORITIES)
            self._require_fact(person_id, "title", role.title_raw)
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM roles WHERE person_id = ?", (person_id,))
        self.conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO roles (person_id, title_raw, function, seniority, is_current)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [(person_id, r.title_raw, r.function, r.seniority, int(r.is_current)) for r in roles],
        )

    def clear_people(self, company_id: int) -> None:
        """Drop people (cascading to roles and facts) before a full re-resolve."""
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM people WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- collection runs

    def start_run(self, company_id: int) -> int:
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO collection_runs (company_id, started_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
            (company_id, utc_now_iso()),
        )
        return cur.lastrowid

    def finish_run(self, run_id: int, stats: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.conn.execute(
            "UPDATE collection_runs SET finished_at = ?, stats_json = ? WHERE id = ?",
            (utc_now_iso(), json.dumps(stats, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True), run_id),
        )

    def latest_run(self, domain: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT cr.* FROM collection_runs cr JOIN companies c ON c.id = cr.company_id
               WHERE c.domain = ? AND cr.finished_at IS NOT NULL
               ORDER BY cr.finished_at DESC, cr.id DESC LIMIT 1""",
            (domain,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        run = dict(row)
        run["stats"] = json.loads(run.pop("stats_json") or "{}")
        return run

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- reads for chat / UI

    def _roles_for(self, person_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        rows = self.conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT title_raw, function, seniority, is_current FROM roles r
                WHERE r.person_id = ? ORDER BY {_SENIORITY_ORDER}, r.title_raw""",
            (person_id,),
        ).fetchall()
        return [dict(r) | {"is_current": bool(r["is_current"])} for r in rows]

    def list_leaders(
        self, domain: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Current leaders with at least one current role matching the filters."""
        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
        rows = self.conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT p.id, p.full_name, p.location, p.confidence, p.profile_url,
                   (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.source_id) FROM facts f WHERE f.person_id = p.id)
                     AS source_count,
                   (SELECT MIN({_SENIORITY_ORDER}) FROM roles r
                     WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1) AS rank
                FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
                WHERE c.domain = ?
                  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM roles r WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1
                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?))
                ORDER BY rank, p.full_name""",
            (domain, function, function, seniority, seniority),
        ).fetchall()
        leaders = []
        for row in rows:
            person = dict(row)
            person.pop("rank")
            person["roles"] = [r for r in self._roles_for(person["id"]) if r["is_current"]]
            leaders.append(person)
        return leaders

    def count_leaders(
        self, domain: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
    ) -> int:
        """Distinct people (not roles) with a current role matching the filters."""
        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
        return self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM people p
               JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
               JOIN roles r ON r.person_id = p.id
               WHERE c.domain = ? AND r.is_current = 1
                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?)""",
            (domain, function, function, seniority, seniority),
        ).fetchone()[0]

    def get_person(self, domain: str, name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """People whose normalized name contains every token of `name`, with facts and sources.

        An exact normalized match wins outright; otherwise all token matches are returned so
        the caller can surface ambiguity instead of picking one.
        """
        query = normalize_name(name)
        if not query:
            return []
        candidates = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT p.* FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
               WHERE c.domain = ? ORDER BY p.full_name""",
            (domain,),
        ).fetchall()
        exact = [p for p in candidates if p["normalized_name"] == query]
        tokens = query.split()
        matches = exact or [
            p for p in candidates if all(t in p["normalized_name"].split() for t in tokens)
        ]
        return [self._person_detail(dict(p)) for p in matches]

    def _person_detail(self, person: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        facts = self.conn.execute(
            """SELECT f.field, f.value, f.evidence_snippet, f.extracted_at,
                      s.id AS source_id, s.url, s.source_type, s.fetched_at
               FROM facts f JOIN sources s ON s.id = f.source_id
               WHERE f.person_id = ? ORDER BY f.field, s.source_type, s.url""",
            (person["id"],),
        ).fetchall()
        person.pop("normalized_name", None)
        person["roles"] = self._roles_for(person["id"])
        person["facts"] = [
            {
                "field": f["field"],
                "value": f["value"],
                "evidence_snippet": f["evidence_snippet"],
                "extracted_at": f["extracted_at"],
                "source": {
                    "url": f["url"],
                    "source_type": f["source_type"],
                    "fetched_at": f["fetched_at"],

import sqlite3

import pytest

from leadership.models import normalize_name
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import ProvenanceError, Repository, RoleIn

DOMAIN = "example.com"


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    conn = connect(tmp_path / "test.db")
    yield Repository(conn)
    conn.close()


def _person(repo, company_id, source_id, name, title, function, seniority, location=None):

    repo.add_fact(pid, "full_name", name, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", title, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    if location:
        repo.add_fact(pid, "location", location, source_id, f"based in {location}")
    repo.update_person_resolved(pid, full_name=name, confidence="high", location=location)
    repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn(title, function, seniority)])
    return pid


@pytest.fixture
def seeded(repo):
    cid = repo.upsert_company("Example", DOMAIN, is_public=True, ticker="EXMP")
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    news = repo.add_source(cid, "https://news.test/a", "search", "2026-01-02", "b")
    ceo = _person(repo, cid, site, "Ada Lovelace", "CEO", "other", "c_level", "London")
    _person(repo, cid, site, "Grace Hopper", "VP of Engineering", "engineering", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Alan Turing", "VP, Marketing", "marketing", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Mary Ann Smith", "Head of Design", "design", "head")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "John Smith", "Head of Sales", "sales", "head")
    # Second source for the CEO, so source_count is 2.
    repo.add_fact(ceo, "title", "CEO", news, "CEO Ada Lovelace said")
    return repo, cid


def test_list_leaders_filters_and_orders(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    names = [p["full_name"] for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)]
    assert names[0] == "Ada Lovelace"  # c_level first
    assert set(names[1:3]) == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}  # then VPs
    vps = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp")
    assert {p["full_name"] for p in vps} == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}
    eng = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="engineering", seniority="vp")
    assert [p["full_name"] for p in eng] == ["Grace Hopper"]
    assert repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="legal") == []
    assert repo.list_leaders("unknown.com") == []

    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp") == 2
    # A person with two current roles still counts once.
    pid = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Ada Lovelace")[0]["id"]
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "Co-founder", site, "Co-founder Ada")
    repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn("CEO", "other", "c_level"), RoleIn("Co-founder", "other", "founder")])
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5


def test_source_count_is_computed(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    by_name = {p["full_name"]: p for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)}
    assert by_name["Ada Lovelace"]["source_count"] == 2
    assert by_name["Grace Hopper"]["source_count"] == 1


def test_get_person_returns_facts_with_sources(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    [ada] = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "ada lovelace")
    assert ada["location"] == "London"
    assert ada["source_count"] == 2
    assert {f["source"]["source_type"] for f in ada["facts"]} == {"company_site", "search"}
    assert all(f["evidence_snippet"] for f in ada["facts"])

    repo, _ = seeded
    assert [p["full_name"] for p in repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Lovelace")] == ["Ada Lovelace"]

    assert smiths == {"John Smith", "Mary Ann Smith"}
    assert repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Nobody") == []
    assert repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "  ") == []


def test_invalid_filter_rejected(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="function"):
        repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="wizardry")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="seniority"):
        repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="intern")


def test_fact_requires_evidence(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    pid = repo.upsert_person(cid, "New Person")
    src = repo.add_source(cid, "https://x.test", "search", "2026-01-01", "c")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "CTO", src, "   ")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "", src, "snippet")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="field"):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "salary", "1", src, "snippet")


def test_resolved_fields_require_backing_fact(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    pid = repo.upsert_person(cid, "New Person")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.update_person_resolved(pid, full_name="New Person", confidence="low", location="Paris")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn("CTO", "engineering", "c_level")])


def test_unique_person_per_normalized_name(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    first = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Grace Hopper")[0]["id"]
    assert repo.upsert_person(cid, "grace  HOPPER") == first
    assert repo.upsert_person(cid, "Dr. Grace M. Hopper") == first


def test_schema_check_constraints(repo):
    cid = repo.upsert_company("X", "x.com")
    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):
        repo.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO sources (company_id, url, source_type, fetched_at, raw_path)"
            " VALUES (?, 'u', 'linkedin', 't', 'p')",
            (cid,),
        )
    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):  # foreign key enforced
        repo.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO roles (person_id, title_raw, function, seniority) VALUES (999, 'a', 'other', 'vp')"
        )


def test_runs_round_trip(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    run = repo.start_run(cid)
    repo.finish_run(run, {"people_found": 5, "cost_usd": 0.12})
    latest = repo.latest_run(DOMAIN)
    assert latest["stats"] == {"cost_usd": 0.12, "people_found": 5}
    assert latest["finished_at"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("a", "b"),
    [
        ("Jason S. Warnick", "jason warnick"),
        ("José Álvarez", "jose alvarez"),
        ("Conor O’Brien", "Conor O'Brien"),
        ("Mary-Kate Lee Jr.", "mary kate lee"),
    ],
)
def test_normalize_name_equivalences(a, b):
    assert normalize_name(a) == normalize_name(b)


def test_normalize_name_keeps_distinct_people_apart():
    assert normalize_name("Vlad Tenev") != normalize_name("Vladimir Tenev")
    assert normalize_name("Mary Ann Smith") != normalize_name("Mary Smith")

import sqlite3

import pytest

from leadership.models import normalize_name
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import ProvenanceError, Repository, RoleIn

DOMAIN = "example.com"


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    conn = connect(tmp_path / "test.db")
    yield Repository(conn)
    conn.close()


def _person(repo, company_id, source_id, name, title, function, seniority, location=None):
    pid = repo.upsert_person(company_id, name)
    repo.add_fact(pid, "full_name", name, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", title, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    if location:
        repo.add_fact(pid, "location", location, source_id, f"based in {location}")
    repo.update_person_resolved(pid, full_name=name, confidence="high", location=location)
    repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn(title, function, seniority)])
    return pid


@pytest.fixture
def seeded(repo):
    cid = repo.upsert_company("Example", DOMAIN, is_public=True, ticker="EXMP")
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    news = repo.add_source(cid, "https://news.test/a", "search", "2026-01-02", "b")
    ceo = _person(repo, cid, site, "Ada Lovelace", "CEO", "other", "c_level", "London")
    _person(repo, cid, site, "Grace Hopper", "VP of Engineering", "engineering", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Alan Turing", "VP, Marketing", "marketing", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Mary Ann Smith", "Head of Design", "design", "head")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "John Smith", "Head of Sales", "sales", "head")
    # Second source for the CEO, so source_count is 2.
    repo.add_fact(ceo, "title", "CEO", news, "CEO Ada Lovelace said")
    return repo, cid


def test_list_leaders_filters_and_orders(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    names = [p["full_name"] for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)]
    assert names[0] == "Ada Lovelace"  # c_level first
    assert set(names[1:3]) == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}  # then VPs
    vps = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp")
    assert {p["full_name"] for p in vps} == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}
    eng = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="engineering", seniority="vp")
    assert [p["full_name"] for p in eng] == ["Grace Hopper"]
    assert repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="legal") == []
    assert repo.list_leaders("unknown.com") == []


def test_count_leaders_counts_people_not_roles(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp") == 2
    # A person with two current roles still counts once.
    pid = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Ada Lovelace")[0]["id"]
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "Co-founder", site, "Co-founder Ada")
    repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn("CEO", "other", "c_level"), RoleIn("Co-founder", "other", "founder")])
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5


def test_source_count_is_computed(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    by_name = {p["full_name"]: p for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)}
    assert by_name["Ada Lovelace"]["source_count"] == 2
    assert by_name["Grace Hopper"]["source_count"] == 1


def test_get_person_returns_facts_with_sources(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    [ada] = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "ada lovelace")
    assert ada["location"] == "London"
    assert ada["source_count"] == 2
    assert {f["source"]["source_type"] for f in ada["facts"]} == {"company_site", "search"}
    assert all(f["evidence_snippet"] for f in ada["facts"])


def test_get_person_partial_and_ambiguous(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded

# Decisions

Each entry: what we chose, what we rejected, and why. Newest at the bottom.

## D1. No LinkedIn as a source

- **Chosen:** The company's own site, SEC EDGAR, and one web search API.
- **Rejected:** Scraping LinkedIn (directly or through scraping proxies or APIs that resell its data).
- **Why:** LinkedIn's User Agreement prohibits scraping. We accept the cost: weaker coverage of VPs and department heads, who often appear only there. That gap is measured (coverage-scout, also LinkedIn-free) and listed under "Known misses" in `VALIDATION.md`. The same rule covers any site whose ToS forbids automated access.

## D2. SQLite relational store, not a vector store

- **Chosen:** SQLite with a plain `schema.sql`, committed per company at `data/<domain>/leadership.db`.
- **Rejected:** A vector store or embedding retrieval over raw pages. Also rejected: Postgres as a runtime dependency.
- **Why:** The target questions are structured: filter by role ("who's the CTO"), count ("how many VPs"), and look up a field ("where is the CEO based"). A relational model answers them exactly, while similarity search makes counts and filters approximate. SQLite needs no server, so the repo stays clone-and-go.
- **Postgres compatibility:** The schema avoids SQLite-only features. Booleans are `INTEGER` 0/1, timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC `TEXT`, and enums are `CHECK` constraints. The one swap is that `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` becomes `id INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY`. Queries in `repository.py` use `?` placeholders, which a Postgres driver would replace with `%s`.

## D3. Resolved view and audit trail are separate tables

- **Chosen:** `facts` stores every claim (field, value, source, evidence snippet). `people` and `roles` store the resolved current view, derived from facts.
- **Rejected:** One `people` table with the source columns inline.
- **Why:** Inline sources can only keep one source per field, so conflicts disappear. With separate facts, the chat agent can show every source and point out disagreements.
- **Enforced in the repository, not just the pipeline:** A fact needs a source and a non-blank snippet (also a DB `CHECK`). `location`, `bio`, and each role's `title_raw` can only be written if a matching fact exists for that person. Otherwise `ProvenanceError` is raised.
- `people.profile_url` holds the URL of a source page (always one we fetched), not a separately sourced claim.

## D4. Schema details (reviewed with Daniel in Phase 0)

- **Source priority is derived, not stored.** `SOURCE_PRIORITY` in `models.py` maps `sources.source_type` to a priority: company_site (0) beats sec_filing (1), which beats search (2). Rejected: a `facts.source_priority` column, which would duplicate `source_type` and could drift from it.
- **`source_count` is computed in the query** (distinct `source_id` across the person's facts). Rejected: storing it on `roles`, where it could go stale after a re-resolve.
- **No `exec` seniority.** President and General Counsel map to `c_level`, because the 10-K lists them as executive officers. `title_raw` always keeps the original title, so nothing is lost. Allowed seniorities: `c_level | vp | head | founder`.
- **Dedupe key:** `people` is unique on `(company_id, normalized_name)`. `normalize_name` strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics and suffixes, and middle initials. It deliberately does **not** merge nicknames ("Vlad" vs "Vladimir"). A wrong merge would combine two people's facts, which is worse than a duplicate that shows up in validation.
- **`facts.field`** is restricted to `full_name | title | location | bio`.
- **`collection_runs.stats_json`** holds tokens in and out, cost, document counts per source, people found, and rejected extractions with reasons.
- **Counts are of people, not roles.** A CEO who is also a co-founder counts once in "how many leaders".

## D5. Configuration via environment

- `.env` at the repo root is loaded automatically (`python-dotenv`). Variables: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `SEC_USER_AGENT` (used as-is, e.g. `"Jane Doe jane@example.com"`, as SEC requires), and `LLM_MODEL` (blank means `claude-sonnet-5-5`).
- Only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is needed to run chat, eval, and the UI against the committed data. `TAVILY_API_KEY` and `SEC_USER_AGENT` are only needed for `leadership collect`. A missing key raises an error that names the variable and says where to get it.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- people / facts / roles

    def upsert_person(self, company_id: int, full_name: str, confidence: str = "low") -> int:
        """Get or create a person by normalized name. Does not overwrite resolved fields."""
        _check_choice("confidence", confidence, CONFIDENCE_LEVELS)
        key = normalize_name(full_name)
        if not key:
            raise ValueError(f"Name {full_name!r} normalizes to an empty string")
        self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO people (company_id, full_name, normalized_name, confidence, updated_at)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
               ON CONFLICT (company_id, normalized_name) DO NOTHING""",
            (company_id, full_name, key, confidence, utc_now_iso()),
        )
        return self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM people WHERE company_id = ? AND normalized_name = ?", (company_id, key)
        ).fetchone()[0]

    def add_fact(
        self,
        person_id: int,
        field: str,
        value: str,
        source_id: int,
        evidence_snippet: str,
        extracted_at: str | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        _check_choice("field", field, FACT_FIELDS)
        if not value or not value.strip():
            raise ProvenanceError(f"Fact {field!r} has an empty value")
        if not evidence_snippet or not evidence_snippet.strip():
            raise ProvenanceError(f"Fact {field}={value!r} has no evidence snippet")
        now = utc_now_iso()
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO facts
                 (person_id, field, value, source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (person_id, field, value.strip(), source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at or now),
        )
        return _lastrowid(cur)

    def _require_fact(self, person_id: int, field: str, value: str) -> None:
        row = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM facts WHERE person_id = ? AND field = ? AND value = ? LIMIT 1",
            (person_id, field, value),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ProvenanceError(f"No {field!r} fact with value {value!r} for person {person_id}")

    def update_person_resolved(
        self,
        person_id: int,
        *,
        full_name: str,
        confidence: str,
        location: str | None = None,
        bio: str | None = None,
        profile_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        _check_choice("confidence", confidence, CONFIDENCE_LEVELS)
        if location is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "location", location)
        if bio is not None:
            self._require_fact(person_id, "bio", bio)
        self.conn.execute(
            """UPDATE people SET full_name = ?, location = ?, bio = ?, profile_url = ?,
                 confidence = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?""",
            (full_name, location, bio, profile_url, confidence, utc_now_iso(), person_id),
        )

    def replace_roles(self, person_id: int, roles: list[RoleIn]) -> None:
        for role in roles:
            _check_choice("function", role.function, FUNCTIONS)
            _check_choice("seniority", role.seniority, SENIORITIES)
            self._require_fact(person_id, "title", role.title_raw)
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM roles WHERE person_id = ?", (person_id,))
        self.conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO roles (person_id, title_raw, function, seniority, is_current)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [(person_id, r.title_raw, r.function, r.seniority, int(r.is_current)) for r in roles],
        )

        """Drop people (cascading to roles and facts) before a full re-resolve."""

import sqlite3

import pytest

from leadership.models import normalize_name
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import ProvenanceError, Repository, RoleIn

DOMAIN = "example.com"


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    conn = connect(tmp_path / "test.db")
    yield Repository(conn)
    conn.close()


def _person(repo, company_id, source_id, name, title, function, seniority, location=None):
    pid = repo.upsert_person(company_id, name)
    repo.add_fact(pid, "full_name", name, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", title, source_id, f"{name}, {title}")
    if location:
        repo.add_fact(pid, "location", location, source_id, f"based in {location}")
    repo.update_person_resolved(pid, full_name=name, confidence="high", location=location)
    repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn(title, function, seniority)])
    return pid


@pytest.fixture
def seeded(repo):
    cid = repo.upsert_company("Example", DOMAIN, is_public=True, ticker="EXMP")
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    news = repo.add_source(cid, "https://news.test/a", "search", "2026-01-02", "b")
    ceo = _person(repo, cid, site, "Ada Lovelace", "CEO", "other", "c_level", "London")
    _person(repo, cid, site, "Grace Hopper", "VP of Engineering", "engineering", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Alan Turing", "VP, Marketing", "marketing", "vp")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "Mary Ann Smith", "Head of Design", "design", "head")
    _person(repo, cid, news, "John Smith", "Head of Sales", "sales", "head")
    # Second source for the CEO, so source_count is 2.
    repo.add_fact(ceo, "title", "CEO", news, "CEO Ada Lovelace said")
    return repo, cid


def test_list_leaders_filters_and_orders(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    names = [p["full_name"] for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)]
    assert names[0] == "Ada Lovelace"  # c_level first
    assert set(names[1:3]) == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}  # then VPs
    vps = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp")
    assert {p["full_name"] for p in vps} == {"Alan Turing", "Grace Hopper"}
    eng = repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="engineering", seniority="vp")
    assert [p["full_name"] for p in eng] == ["Grace Hopper"]
    assert repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="legal") == []
    assert repo.list_leaders("unknown.com") == []


def test_count_leaders_counts_people_not_roles(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="vp") == 2
    # A person with two current roles still counts once.
    pid = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Ada Lovelace")[0]["id"]
    site = repo.add_source(cid, "https://example.com/team", "company_site", "2026-01-01", "a")
    repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "Co-founder", site, "Co-founder Ada")
    repo.replace_roles(
        pid, [RoleIn("CEO", "other", "c_level"), RoleIn("Co-founder", "other", "founder")]
    )
    assert repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN) == 5


def test_source_count_is_computed(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    by_name = {p["full_name"]: p for p in repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN)}
    assert by_name["Ada Lovelace"]["source_count"] == 2
    assert by_name["Grace Hopper"]["source_count"] == 1


def test_get_person_returns_facts_with_sources(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    [ada] = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "ada lovelace")
    assert ada["location"] == "London"
    assert ada["source_count"] == 2
    assert {f["source"]["source_type"] for f in ada["facts"]} == {"company_site", "search"}
    assert all(f["evidence_snippet"] for f in ada["facts"])


def test_get_person_partial_and_ambiguous(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    assert [p["full_name"] for p in repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Lovelace")] == ["Ada Lovelace"]
    smiths = {p["full_name"] for p in repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Smith")}
    assert smiths == {"John Smith", "Mary Ann Smith"}
    assert repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Nobody") == []
    assert repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "  ") == []


def test_invalid_filter_rejected(seeded):
    repo, _ = seeded
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="function"):
        repo.list_leaders(DOMAIN, function="wizardry")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="seniority"):
        repo.count_leaders(DOMAIN, seniority="intern")


def test_fact_requires_evidence(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    pid = repo.upsert_person(cid, "New Person")
    src = repo.add_source(cid, "https://x.test", "search", "2026-01-01", "c")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "CTO", src, "   ")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "title", "", src, "snippet")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="field"):
        repo.add_fact(pid, "salary", "1", src, "snippet")


def test_resolved_fields_require_backing_fact(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    pid = repo.upsert_person(cid, "New Person")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.update_person_resolved(pid, full_name="New Person", confidence="low", location="Paris")
    with pytest.raises(ProvenanceError):
        repo.replace_roles(pid, [RoleIn("CTO", "engineering", "c_level")])


def test_unique_person_per_normalized_name(seeded):
    repo, cid = seeded
    first = repo.get_person(DOMAIN, "Grace Hopper")[0]["id"]
    assert repo.upsert_person(cid, "grace  HOPPER") == first
    assert repo.upsert_person(cid, "Dr. Grace M. Hopper") == first

# Decisions

Each entry: what we chose, what we rejected, and why. Newest at the bottom.

## D1. No LinkedIn as a source

- **Chosen:** The company's own site, SEC EDGAR, and one web search API.
- **Rejected:** Scraping LinkedIn (directly or through scraping proxies or APIs that resell its data).
- **Why:** LinkedIn's User Agreement prohibits scraping. We accept the cost: weaker coverage of VPs and department heads, who often appear only there. That gap is measured (coverage-scout, also LinkedIn-free) and listed under "Known misses" in `VALIDATION.md`. The same rule covers any site whose ToS forbids automated access.

## D2. SQLite relational store, not a vector store

- **Chosen:** SQLite with a plain `schema.sql`, committed per company at `data/<domain>/leadership.db`.
- **Rejected:** A vector store or embedding retrieval over raw pages. Also rejected: Postgres as a runtime dependency.
- **Why:** The target questions are structured: filter by role ("who's the CTO"), count ("how many VPs"), and look up a field ("where is the CEO based"). A relational model answers them exactly, while similarity search makes counts and filters approximate. SQLite needs no server, so the repo stays clone-and-go.
- **Postgres compatibility:** The schema avoids SQLite-only features. Booleans are `INTEGER` 0/1, timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC `TEXT`, and enums are `CHECK` constraints. The one swap is that `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` becomes `id INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY`. Queries in `repository.py` use `?` placeholders, which a Postgres driver would replace with `%s`.

## D3. Resolved view and audit trail are separate tables

- **Chosen:** `facts` stores every claim (field, value, source, evidence snippet). `people` and `roles` store the resolved current view, derived from facts.
- **Rejected:** One `people` table with the source columns inline.
- **Why:** Inline sources can only keep one source per field, so conflicts disappear. With separate facts, the chat agent can show every source and point out disagreements.
- **Enforced in the repository, not just the pipeline:** A fact needs a source and a non-blank snippet (also a DB `CHECK`). `location`, `bio`, and each role's `title_raw` can only be written if a matching fact exists for that person. Otherwise `ProvenanceError` is raised.
- `people.profile_url` holds the URL of a source page (always one we fetched), not a separately sourced claim.

## D4. Schema details (reviewed with Daniel in Phase 0)

- **Source priority is derived, not stored.** `SOURCE_PRIORITY` in `models.py` maps `sources.source_type` to a priority: company_site (0) beats sec_filing (1), which beats search (2). Rejected: a `facts.source_priority` column, which would duplicate `source_type` and could drift from it.
- **`source_count` is computed in the query** (distinct `source_id` across the person's facts). Rejected: storing it on `roles`, where it could go stale after a re-resolve.
- **No `exec` seniority.** President and General Counsel map to `c_level`, because the 10-K lists them as executive officers. `title_raw` always keeps the original title, so nothing is lost. Allowed seniorities: `c_level | vp | head | founder`.
- **Dedupe key:** `people` is unique on `(company_id, normalized_name)`. `normalize_name` strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics and suffixes, and middle initials. It deliberately does **not** merge nicknames ("Vlad" vs "Vladimir"). A wrong merge would combine two people's facts, which is worse than a duplicate that shows up in validation.
- **`facts.field`** is restricted to `full_name | title | location | bio`.
- **`collection_runs.stats_json`** holds tokens in and out, cost, document counts per source, people found, and rejected extractions with reasons.
- **Counts are of people, not roles.** A CEO who is also a co-founder counts once in "how many leaders".

## D5. Configuration via environment

- `.env` at the repo root is loaded automatically (`python-dotenv`). Variables: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `SEC_USER_AGENT` (used as-is, e.g. `"Jane Doe jane@example.com"`, as SEC requires), and `LLM_MODEL` (blank means `claude-sonnet-5-5`).
- Only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is needed to run chat, eval, and the UI against the committed data. `TAVILY_API_KEY` and `SEC_USER_AGENT` are only needed for `leadership collect`. A missing key raises an error that names the variable and says where to get it.

  - a person is created together with a `full_name` fact, so a person can't exist without a source and an evidence snippet;
  - a location, bio, role title or the final name can only be set if a matching fact exists;
  - every source must belong to the same company;
  - `profile_url` must be a page we actually fetched.
- The three chat lookups are ready: `list_leaders`, `count_leaders` and `get_person`. `get_person` returns every match for an ambiguous name like "Smith" rather than picking one, so the chat agent can ask which person you mean.
