1	"""Deterministic resolution of extracted people (no LLM).
2	
3	This module currently holds the identity rule: deciding whether two name records for the
4	same company are the same person. Phase 3 adds fact writing and conflict resolution here.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
10	from difflib import SequenceMatcher
11	from enum import StrEnum
12	
13	from leadership.models import normalize_name
14	
15	# Small, explicit nickname map. Keys and values are normalized (lowercase, no accents).
16	# Prefix pairs ("vlad"/"vladimir", "dan"/"daniel") don't need an entry; see _first_names_match.
17	_NICKNAME_GROUPS = (
18	    {"robert", "rob", "bob", "bobby", "robbie"},
19	    {"william", "will", "bill", "billy", "liam"},
20	    {"james", "jim", "jimmy", "jamie"},
21	    {"michael", "mike", "mick"},
22	    {"richard", "rick", "dick", "rich"},
23	    {"edward", "ed", "eddie", "ted", "ned"},
24	    {"elizabeth", "liz", "beth", "betsy", "eliza"},
25	    {"margaret", "maggie", "peggy", "meg"},
26	    {"katherine", "catherine", "kate", "katie", "kathy", "cathy"},
27	    {"anthony", "tony"},
28	    {"andrew", "andy", "drew"},
29	    {"steven", "stephen", "steve"},
30	    {"joseph", "joe", "joey"},
31	    {"thomas", "tom", "tommy"},
32	    {"charles", "charlie", "chuck"},
33	    {"john", "jack", "johnny"},
34	    {"alexander", "alexandra", "alex", "sasha"},
35	    {"jennifer", "jen", "jenny"},
36	    {"christopher", "chris"},
37	    {"susan", "sue", "suzy"},
38	)
39	_NICKNAMES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
40	    name: frozenset(group) for group in _NICKNAME_GROUPS for name in group
41	}
42	
43	# A prefix shorter than this is too ambiguous to merge on ("Al" could be Alan or Alice).
44	_MIN_PREFIX_LEN = 3
45	# Whole-name similarity at or above this, without a merge, is flagged for human review.
46	_POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE_RATIO = 0.85
47	# Same first initial plus last names at least this similar is also flagged.
48	_SIMILAR_LAST_NAME_RATIO = 0.8
49	
50	
51	def _ratio(a: str, b: str) -> float:
52	    return SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()
53	
54	
55	class Identity(StrEnum):
56	    SAME = "same"  # merge automatically
57	    POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE = "possible_duplicate"  # keep separate, list in VALIDATION.md
58	    DIFFERENT = "different"
59	
60	
61	@dataclass(frozen=True)
62	class NameRecord:
63	    company_id: int
64	    full_name: str
65	    functions: frozenset[str] = field(default_factory=frozenset)
66	
67	    @property
68	    def tokens(self) -> list[str]:
69	        return normalize_name(self.full_name).split()
70	
71	
72	def _first_names_match(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
73	    if a == b:
74	        return True
75	    short, long = sorted((a, b), key=len)
76	    if len(short) >= _MIN_PREFIX_LEN and long.startswith(short):
77	        return True
78	    return b in _NICKNAMES.get(a, frozenset())
79	
80	
81	def compare_identity(a: NameRecord, b: NameRecord) -> Identity:
82	    """Narrow, deterministic same-person rule.
83	
84	    SAME only when all hold: same company; identical normalized names, OR same last name +
85	    first names that match by prefix (Vlad/Vladimir) or the nickname map + at least one
86	    overlapping role function. Anything close that misses a condition is
87	    POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE so a human decides; a wrong merge would mix two people's facts.
88	    """
89	    if a.company_id != b.company_id:
90	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
91	    ta, tb = a.tokens, b.tokens
92	    if not ta or not tb:
93	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
94	    if ta == tb:
95	        return Identity.SAME
96	
97	    same_last = ta[-1] == tb[-1]
98	    first_match = _first_names_match(ta[0], tb[0])
99	    function_overlap = bool(a.functions & b.functions)
100	
101	    if same_last and first_match and function_overlap:
102	        return Identity.SAME
103	    same_initial = ta[0][0] == tb[0][0]
104	    if same_last and (first_match or same_initial):
105	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
106	    if same_initial and _ratio(ta[-1], tb[-1]) >= _SIMILAR_LAST_NAME_RATIO:
107	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE  # e.g. Quirk / Quirke
108	    ratio = _ratio(" ".join(ta), " ".join(tb))
109	    if ratio >= _POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE_RATIO:
110	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
111	    return Identity.DIFFERENT

"""Keyword pre-filter (no LLM): which parts of a document are worth sending to the model.

Pages are long (nav, footers, product copy); leaders appear in a few lines. We keep windows of
lines around leadership keywords and skip documents with no hit at all, so the LLM sees less
text and costs less. The evidence check (validate.py) still runs against the *full* text.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from leadership.sources.base import RawDocument

KEYWORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:chief\s+\w+(?:\s+\w+){0,4}\s+officer|ceo|cfo|cto|coo|cmo|cpo|ciso|cro|clo|chro|cio"
    r"|president|vice\s+president|vp|svp|evp|head\s+of|general\s+counsel|co-?founder|founder"
    r"|executive\s+officers?|leadership|management\s+team|appoint\w*|hires?|hired|names?|named"
    r"|joins?|joined|promot\w+)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# A line that looks like a role line on its own ("Head of Product", "CEO & Founder").
_ROLE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:chief|officer|ceo|cfo|cto|coo|president|vice president|vp|head of|founder|counsel)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WINDOW_LINES = 3
MAX_CHARS = 24_000  # per document sent to the model; the rest is dropped with a note


def select_text(doc: RawDocument) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(text for the model, note). Empty text means: no leadership signal, skip the LLM."""
    text = doc.text
    if doc.source_type == "sec_filing":
        span = doc.meta.get("executive_officers_span")
        if span:
            return text[span[0] : span[1]], "SEC executive officers section"
        sig = text.rfind("SIGNATURES")
        if sig >= 0:
            return text[sig : sig + MAX_CHARS], "SEC signatures section"
        return "", "SEC filing without an executive officers or signatures section"

    lines = text.splitlines()
    keep: set[int] = set()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _ROLE_LINE.search(line) or KEYWORDS.search(line) and _ROLE_LINE.search(
            " ".join(lines[max(0, i - 2) : i + 3])
        ):
            keep.update(range(max(0, i - WINDOW_LINES), min(len(lines), i + WINDOW_LINES + 1)))
    if not keep:
        return "", "no leadership keywords"

    chunks: list[str] = []
    prev = -2
    for i in sorted(keep):
        if i != prev + 1 and chunks:
            chunks.append("[...]")
        chunks.append(lines[i])
        prev = i
    selected = "\n".join(chunks)
    note = f"{len(keep)} of {len(lines)} lines"
    if len(selected) > MAX_CHARS:
        selected = selected[:MAX_CHARS]
        note += f", truncated to {MAX_CHARS} chars"
    return selected, note

"""Keyword pre-filter (no LLM): which parts of a document are worth sending to the model.

Pages are long (nav, footers, product copy); leaders appear in a few lines. We keep windows of
lines around leadership keywords and skip documents with no hit at all, so the LLM sees less
text and costs less. The evidence check (validate.py) still runs against the *full* text.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from leadership.sources.base import RawDocument

KEYWORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:chief\s+\w+(?:\s+\w+){0,4}\s+officer|ceo|cfo|cto|coo|cmo|cpo|ciso|cro|clo|chro|cio"
    r"|president|vice\s+president|vp|svp|evp|head\s+of|general\s+counsel|co-?founder|founder"
    r"|executive\s+officers?|leadership|management\s+team|appoint\w*|hires?|hired|names?|named"
    r"|joins?|joined|promot\w+)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# A line that looks like a role line on its own ("Head of Product", "CEO & Founder").
_ROLE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:chief|officer|ceo|cfo|cto|coo|president|vice president|vp|head of|founder|counsel)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WINDOW_LINES = 3
MAX_CHARS = 24_000  # per document sent to the model; the rest is dropped with a note


def select_text(doc: RawDocument) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(text for the model, note). Empty text means: no leadership signal, skip the LLM."""
    text = doc.text
    if doc.source_type == "sec_filing":
        span = doc.meta.get("executive_officers_span")
        if span:
            return text[span[0] : span[1]], "SEC executive officers section"
        sig = text.rfind("SIGNATURES")
        if sig >= 0:
            return text[sig : sig + MAX_CHARS], "SEC signatures section"
        return "", "SEC filing without an executive officers or signatures section"

    lines = text.splitlines()
    keep: set[int] = set()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _ROLE_LINE.search(line) or KEYWORDS.search(line) and _ROLE_LINE.search(
            " ".join(lines[max(0, i - 2) : i + 3])
        ):
            keep.update(range(max(0, i - WINDOW_LINES), min(len(lines), i + WINDOW_LINES + 1)))
    if not keep:
        return "", "no leadership keywords"

    chunks: list[str] = []
    prev = -2
    for i in sorted(keep):
        if i != prev + 1 and chunks:
            chunks.append("[...]")
        chunks.append(lines[i])
        prev = i
    selected = "\n".join(chunks)
    note = f"{len(keep)} of {len(lines)} lines"
    if len(selected) > MAX_CHARS:
        selected = selected[:MAX_CHARS]
        note += f", truncated to {MAX_CHARS} chars"
    return selected, note

"""LLM extraction: one structured-output call per pre-filtered document.

The model only *reads*: it returns people with verbatim evidence. Everything that decides what
is stored (evidence check, title rules, dedupe, currency, confidence) is deterministic code in
validate.py and resolve.py. Responses are cached on disk (keyed by model, prompt version and
the exact input), so re-running resolution costs nothing; `--reextract` ignores the cache.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import logging
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import anthropic
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from leadership.config import require_setting
from leadership.sources.base import Company, RawDocument

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PROMPT_VERSION = "1"
MAX_TOKENS = 16_000
EFFORT = "medium"
WORKERS = 4
# USD per million tokens (input, output). Unknown models are still run; cost is reported null.
PRICES = {
    "claude-sonnet-5-5": (2.00, 10.00),
    "claude-sonnet-5": (2.00, 10.00),
    "claude-opus-5-5": (4.00, 20.00),
    "claude-haiku-5-5": (0.10, 0.50),
}


class ExtractedPerson(BaseModel):
    full_name: str = Field(description="The person's name exactly as written on the page.")
    title: str = Field(
        description="Their job title copied verbatim from the evidence snippet, without the "
        "company name. Example: 'Chief Financial Officer', 'VP, Engineering', 'Head of Product'."
    )
    employer: str = Field(description="Organization this title is held at, as the page says it.")
    works_at_target_company: bool = Field(
        description="True only if the title is held at the target company (not a customer, "
        "investor, partner, previous employer, or a different organization with a similar name)."
    )
    status: Literal["current", "former", "incoming", "unclear"] = Field(
        description="'former' if the page says they left, were replaced, or uses 'former'/'ex-'/"
        "'previously'; 'incoming' if announced but not started; 'current' only if the page "
        "presents the title as held now (as of the page date)."
    )
    evidence_snippet: str = Field(
        description="A verbatim quote from the page (one or two sentences, under 300 "
        "characters) that contains both the person's name and the title."
    )
    location: str | None = Field(
        description="City/region where the person is based, only if the page states it; else null."
    )
    location_snippet: str | None = Field(
        description="Verbatim quote stating the location; null when location is null."
    )
    bio: str | None = Field(
        description="One verbatim sentence from the page describing their background; else null."
    )


class Extraction(BaseModel):
    page_published_date: str | None = Field(
        description="Publication date shown on the page, as YYYY-MM-DD; null if none is shown."
    )
    published_date_snippet: str | None = Field(
        description="The verbatim text on the page that shows that date; null if none."
    )
    people: list[ExtractedPerson]


SYSTEM = """You extract company leadership from one web page or filing. You read; you never guess.

Rules:
- Target company: {name} (website {domain}). Only include people whose title is held AT the target company. Exclude people at other organizations that share the name, customers, investors, partners, authors of quoted studies, and people from other companies mentioned in the text.
- In scope: C-level officers (Chief ... Officer, CEO, CFO, President, General Counsel), founders, Vice Presidents (VP, SVP, EVP), and Heads of a function (Head of X). Skip board-only directors, managers, engineers, and other staff.
- Every value must be copied verbatim from the page text: name, title, snippet, location, bio, date. Do not translate, expand abbreviations, or fix typos. If something is not stated, use null.
- The evidence_snippet must contain both the name and the title, exactly as they appear.
- Mark status 'former' whenever the page says the person left, was replaced, or held the role in the past ("former CFO", "previously VP"). A page that announces an appointment presents it as current as of the page date.
- If the page lists no in-scope people at the target company, return an empty list.
- Text marked [...] was removed by a filter; only use what you see."""


@dataclass
class ExtractResult:
    doc: RawDocument
    extraction: Extraction | None
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    from_cache: bool = False
    error: str = ""


@dataclass
class ExtractStats:
    llm_calls: int = 0
    cached: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    errors: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)

    def cost_usd(self, model: str) -> float | None:
        price = PRICES.get(model)
        if price is None:
            return None
        return round((self.input_tokens * price[0] + self.output_tokens * price[1]) / 1e6, 4)


def _user_prompt(doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> str:
    meta_date = doc.meta.get("published_date") or doc.meta.get("filing_date") or "unknown"
    return (
        f"Source URL: {doc.url}\nPage title: {doc.title}\n"
        f"Publication date from metadata (may be missing): {meta_date}\n\n"
        f"<page>\n{text}\n</page>"
    )


class Extractor:
    def __init__(self, company: Company, model: str, cache_dir: Path, reextract: bool = False):
        self.company = company
        self.model = model
        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
        self.reextract = reextract
        self.system = SYSTEM.format(name=company.name, domain=company.domain)
        self._client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None

    def _client_lazy(self) -> anthropic.Anthropic:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))
        return self._client

    def _cache_path(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> Path:
        key = hashlib.sha256(
            "\x00".join([self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self.system, doc.url, text]).encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()[:24]
        return self.cache_dir / f"{key}.json"

    def extract(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> ExtractResult:
        path = self._cache_path(doc, text)
        if path.exists() and not self.reextract:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            return ExtractResult(
                doc, Extraction.model_validate(data["extraction"]), from_cache=True
            )
        try:
            response = self._client_lazy().messages.parse(
                model=self.model,
                max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
                system=self.system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": _user_prompt(doc, text)}],
                output_format=Extraction,
                output_config={"effort": EFFORT},
            )
        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
        except anthropic.APIError as exc:
            log.warning("extraction failed for %s: %s", doc.url, exc)
            return ExtractResult(doc, None, error=f"API error: {exc}")
        usage = response.usage
        result = ExtractResult(doc, None, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens)
        if response.stop_reason in ("refusal", "max_tokens") or response.parsed_output is None:
            result.error = f"no structured output (stop_reason={response.stop_reason})"
            return result
        result.extraction = response.parsed_output
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            "url": doc.url,
            "model": self.model,
            "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
            "usage": {"input_tokens": usage.input_tokens, "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens},
            "extraction": result.extraction.model_dump(),
        }
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        return result

    def extract_all(
        self, jobs: list[tuple[RawDocument, str]]
    ) -> tuple[list[ExtractResult], ExtractStats]:
        stats = ExtractStats()
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda job: self.extract(*job), jobs))
        for r in results:
            if r.from_cache:
                stats.cached += 1
            else:
                stats.llm_calls += 1
            stats.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
            stats.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
            if r.error:
                stats.errors.append({"url": r.doc.url, "error": r.error})
        return results, stats

    def __init__(self, company: Company, model: str, cache_dir: Path, reextract: bool = False):
        self.company = company
        self.model = model
        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
        self.reextract = reextract
        self.system = SYSTEM.format(name=company.name, domain=company.domain)
        self._client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None

    def _client_lazy(self) -> anthropic.Anthropic:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))
        return self._client

    def _cache_path(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> Path:
        key = hashlib.sha256(
            "\x00".join([self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self.system, doc.url, text]).encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()[:24]
        return self.cache_dir / f"{key}.json"

    def extract(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> ExtractResult:
        path = self._cache_path(doc, text)
        if path.exists() and not self.reextract:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            return ExtractResult(
                doc, Extraction.model_validate(data["extraction"]), from_cache=True
            )
        try:
            response = self._client_lazy().messages.parse(
                model=self.model,
                max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
                system=self.system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": _user_prompt(doc, text)}],
                output_format=Extraction,
                output_config={"effort": EFFORT},
            )
        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
        except anthropic.APIError as exc:
            log.warning("extraction failed for %s: %s", doc.url, exc)
            return ExtractResult(doc, None, error=f"API error: {exc}")
        usage = response.usage
        result = ExtractResult(doc, None, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens)
        if response.stop_reason in ("refusal", "max_tokens") or response.parsed_output is None:
            result.error = f"no structured output (stop_reason={response.stop_reason})"
            return result
        result.extraction = response.parsed_output
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            "url": doc.url,
            "model": self.model,
            "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
            "usage": {"input_tokens": usage.input_tokens, "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens},
            "extraction": result.extraction.model_dump(),
        }
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        return result

    def extract_all(
        self, jobs: list[tuple[RawDocument, str]]
    ) -> tuple[list[ExtractResult], ExtractStats]:
        stats = ExtractStats()
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda job: self.extract(*job), jobs))
        for r in results:
            if r.from_cache:
                stats.cached += 1
            else:
                stats.llm_calls += 1
            stats.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
            stats.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
            if r.error:
                stats.errors.append({"url": r.doc.url, "error": r.error})
        return results, stats

"""Full collection run: discover -> pre-filter -> extract (LLM) -> validate -> resolve -> store.

Writes data/<domain>/leadership.db (rebuilt each run, D3) and data/<domain>/leadership.json,
a readable export of the same data. Both are committed; the raw cache is not (D14).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from leadership.config import company_dir, db_path, llm_model
from leadership.pipeline.discover import discover, fetcher_for, normalize_domain, resolve_company
from leadership.pipeline.extract import PROMPT_VERSION, Extractor
from leadership.pipeline.prefilter import select_text
from leadership.pipeline.resolve import Resolution, ResolvedPerson, resolve_claims
from leadership.pipeline.validate import Claim, Rejection, validate
from leadership.sources.base import Company
from leadership.sources.company_site import MAX_PAGES
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import Repository, RoleIn

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class CollectResult:
    company: Company
    resolution: Resolution
    stats: dict[str, Any]
    db_path: Path
    json_path: Path


def collect(
    url: str,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    ticker: str | None = None,
    private: bool = False,
    max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES,
    refresh: bool = False,
    reextract: bool = False,
    today: date | None = None,
) -> CollectResult:
    started = time.monotonic()
    domain = normalize_domain(url)
    with fetcher_for(domain, refresh) as fetcher:
        company = resolve_company(fetcher, url, name, ticker, private)
        found = discover(company, fetcher, max_pages=max_pages)

    jobs, prefilter_skipped = [], []
    for doc in found.documents:
        text, note = select_text(doc)
        if text:
            jobs.append((doc, text))
        else:
            prefilter_skipped.append({"url": doc.url, "reason": note})
    log.info("%d documents, %d sent to the LLM", len(found.documents), len(jobs))

    model = llm_model()
    extractor = Extractor(company, model, company_dir(domain) / "raw" / "_extractions", reextract)
    results, xstats = extractor.extract_all(jobs)

    claims: list[Claim] = []
    rejections: list[Rejection] = []
    for r in results:
        if r.extraction is not None:
            c, rj = validate(r.doc, r.extraction)
            claims += c
            rejections += rj
    resolution = resolve_claims(claims, today=today)

    stats: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": model,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
        "discovery": found.stats,
        "documents": len(found.documents),
        "documents_sent_to_llm": len(jobs),
        "prefilter_skipped": len(prefilter_skipped),
        "llm_calls": xstats.llm_calls,
        "llm_cached_responses": xstats.cached,
        "tokens_in": xstats.input_tokens,
        "tokens_out": xstats.output_tokens,
        "cost_usd": xstats.cost_usd(model),
        "cost_usd_including_cached": xstats.cost_usd(model, include_cached=True),
        "extraction_errors": xstats.errors,
        "claims_accepted": len(claims),
        "claims_rejected": len(rejections),
        "rejections": [vars(r) for r in rejections],
        "people_found": len(resolution.people),
        "people_current": sum(p.is_current for p in resolution.people),
        "review": resolution.review,
        "duration_s": 0.0,
    }
    path = db_path(domain)
    _store(path, company, resolution, stats, started)
    json_path = export_json(path, domain)
    return CollectResult(company, resolution, stats, path, json_path)


def _store(
    path: Path, company: Company, resolution: Resolution, stats: dict, started: float
) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect(path)
    repo = Repository(conn)
    try:
        with repo.transaction():
            company_id = repo.upsert_company(
                company.name, company.domain, company.is_public, company.ticker
            )
            run_id = repo.start_run(company_id)
            repo.clear_people(company_id)
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM sources WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
            for person in resolution.people:
                _store_person(repo, company_id, person)
            stats["duration_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
            repo.finish_run(run_id, stats)
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _source_id(repo: Repository, company_id: int, claim: Claim, cache: dict[str, int]) -> int:
    doc = claim.doc
    if doc.url not in cache:
        cache[doc.url] = repo.add_source(
            company_id, doc.url, doc.source_type, doc.fetched_at, doc.raw_path, claim.published_at
        )
    return cache[doc.url]


def _store_person(repo: Repository, company_id: int, person: ResolvedPerson) -> None:
    sources: dict[str, int] = {}
    first = person.claims[0]
    best = next(c for c in person.claims if c.full_name == person.full_name)
    person_id = repo.upsert_person(
        company_id,
        person.full_name,
        _source_id(repo, company_id, best, sources),
        best.evidence_snippet,
    )
    for c in person.claims:
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, c, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "full_name", c.full_name, sid, c.evidence_snippet)
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id, "title", c.title, sid, c.evidence_snippet, is_current=c.status != "former"
        )
    if person.location_claim is not None and person.location_claim.location_snippet:
        lc = person.location_claim
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id,
            "location",
            person.location or "",
            _source_id(repo, company_id, lc, sources),
            lc.location_snippet or "",
        )
    if person.bio_claim is not None and person.bio:
        bc = person.bio_claim
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, bc, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "bio", person.bio, sid, person.bio)
    repo.replace_roles(
        person_id,
        [
            RoleIn(r.title, r.function, r.seniority, r.is_current, r.as_of, r.note or None)
            for r in person.roles
        ],
    )
    del first
    repo.update_person_resolved(
        person_id,
        full_name=person.full_name,
        confidence=person.confidence,
        location=person.location,
        bio=person.bio,
        profile_url=person.profile_url,
    )


def export_json(path: Path, domain: str) -> Path:
    """Readable, diff-friendly export of the stored data (committed next to the DB)."""
    conn = connect(path)
    try:
        repo = Repository(conn)
        company = repo.get_company(domain) or {}
        ids = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT p.id FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id "
            "WHERE c.domain = ? ORDER BY p.full_name",
            (domain,),
        )]  # fmt: skip
        people = []
        for pid in ids:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM people WHERE id = ?", (pid,)).fetchone()
            detail = repo._person_detail(dict(row))
            detail.pop("company_id", None)
            people.append(detail)
        run = repo.latest_run(domain)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    out = {"company": company, "latest_run": run, "people": people}
    json_path = path.with_name("leadership.json")
    json_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    return json_path

        if r.extraction is not None:
            c, rj = validate(r.doc, r.extraction)
            claims += c
            rejections += rj
    resolution = resolve_claims(claims, today=today)

    stats: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": model,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
        "discovery": found.stats,
        "documents": len(found.documents),
        "documents_sent_to_llm": len(jobs),
        "prefilter_skipped": len(prefilter_skipped),
        "llm_calls": xstats.llm_calls,
        "llm_cached_responses": xstats.cached,
        "tokens_in": xstats.input_tokens,
        "tokens_out": xstats.output_tokens,
        "cost_usd": xstats.cost_usd(model),
        "cost_usd_including_cached": xstats.cost_usd(model, include_cached=True),
        "extraction_errors": xstats.errors,
        "claims_accepted": len(claims),
        "claims_rejected": len(rejections),
        "rejections": [vars(r) for r in rejections],
        "people_found": len(resolution.people),
        "people_current": sum(p.is_current for p in resolution.people),
        "review": resolution.review,
        "duration_s": 0.0,
    }
    path = db_path(domain)
    _store(path, company, resolution, stats, started)
    json_path = export_json(path, domain)
    return CollectResult(company, resolution, stats, path, json_path)


def _store(
    path: Path, company: Company, resolution: Resolution, stats: dict, started: float
) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect(path)
    repo = Repository(conn)
    try:
        with repo.transaction():
            company_id = repo.upsert_company(
                company.name, company.domain, company.is_public, company.ticker
            )
            run_id = repo.start_run(company_id)
            repo.clear_people(company_id)
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM sources WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
            for person in resolution.people:
                _store_person(repo, company_id, person)
            stats["duration_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
            repo.finish_run(run_id, stats)
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _source_id(repo: Repository, company_id: int, claim: Claim, cache: dict[str, int]) -> int:
    doc = claim.doc
    if doc.url not in cache:
        cache[doc.url] = repo.add_source(
            company_id, doc.url, doc.source_type, doc.fetched_at, doc.raw_path, claim.published_at
        )
    return cache[doc.url]


def _store_person(repo: Repository, company_id: int, person: ResolvedPerson) -> None:
    sources: dict[str, int] = {}
    first = person.claims[0]
    best = next(c for c in person.claims if c.full_name == person.full_name)
    person_id = repo.upsert_person(
        company_id,
        person.full_name,
        _source_id(repo, company_id, best, sources),
        best.evidence_snippet,
    )
    for c in person.claims:
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, c, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "full_name", c.full_name, sid, c.evidence_snippet)
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id, "title", c.title, sid, c.evidence_snippet, is_current=c.status != "former"
        )
    if person.location_claim is not None and person.location_claim.location_snippet:
        lc = person.location_claim
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id,
            "location",
            person.location or "",
            _source_id(repo, company_id, lc, sources),
            lc.location_snippet or "",
        )
    if person.bio_claim is not None and person.bio:
        bc = person.bio_claim
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, bc, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "bio", person.bio, sid, person.bio)
    repo.replace_roles(
        person_id,
        [
            RoleIn(r.title, r.function, r.seniority, r.is_current, r.as_of, r.note or None)
            for r in person.roles
        ],
    )
    del first
    repo.update_person_resolved(
        person_id,
        full_name=person.full_name,
        confidence=person.confidence,
        location=person.location,
        bio=person.bio,
        profile_url=person.profile_url,
    )


def export_json(path: Path, domain: str) -> Path:
    """Readable, diff-friendly export of the stored data (committed next to the DB)."""
    conn = connect(path)
    try:
        repo = Repository(conn)
        company = repo.get_company(domain) or {}
        ids = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT p.id FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id "
            "WHERE c.domain = ? ORDER BY p.full_name",
            (domain,),
        )]  # fmt: skip
        people = []
        for pid in ids:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM people WHERE id = ?", (pid,)).fetchone()
            detail = repo._person_detail(dict(row))
            detail.pop("company_id", None)
            people.append(detail)
        run = repo.latest_run(domain)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    out = {"company": company, "latest_run": run, "people": people}
    json_path = path.with_name("leadership.json")
    json_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    return json_path

        published_date_snippet=None,
        people=[
            person("Vladimir Tenev", "Chair and Chief Executive Officer",
                   "Vladimir Tenev 39 Chair and Chief Executive Officer"),
            person("Shiv Verma", "Chief Financial Officer",
                   "Shiv Verma 41 Chief Financial Officer"),
            # The model is asked for status; even if it says 'current', the snippet says former.
            person("Jason Warnick", "Chief Financial Officer",
                   "Jason Warnick, former Chief Financial Officer.", status="current"),
        ],
    )  # fmt: skip
    claims, rejections = validate(d, ex)
    assert not rejections
    return claims


def news_claims() -> list[Claim]:
    d = doc("https://robinhood.test/news/2021", NEWS_TEXT)
    ex = Extraction(
        page_published_date="2021-03-01",
        published_date_snippet="March 1, 2021",
        people=[
            person("Jason Warnick", "Chief Financial Officer",
                   "Robinhood names Jason Warnick Chief Financial Officer."),
            person("Gretchen Howard", "Chief Operating Officer",
                   "Robinhood names Gretchen Howard Chief Operating Officer."),
            person("Vlad Tenev", "Chief Executive Officer",
                   "Robinhood names Vlad Tenev Chief Executive Officer."),
        ],
    )  # fmt: skip
    claims, rejections = validate(d, ex)
    assert not rejections
    return claims


def by_name(resolution, name):
    return next(p for p in resolution.people if p.full_name == name)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- title rules


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("title", "seniority", "function"),
    [
        ("Chair and Chief Executive Officer", "c_level", "other"),
        ("Chief Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs Officer", "c_level", "legal"),
        ("Chief Brokerage Officer", "c_level", "operations"),
        ("CFO", "c_level", "finance"),
        ("President", "c_level", "other"),
        ("General Counsel", "c_level", "legal"),
        ("SVP, Engineering", "vp", "engineering"),
        ("Vice President of Product", "vp", "product"),
        ("Head of Product", "head", "product"),
        ("Head of People", "head", "people"),
        ("Co-founder", "founder", "other"),
    ],
)
def test_classify_title(title, seniority, function):
    tc = classify_title(title)
    assert tc is not None and (tc.seniority, tc.function) == (seniority, function)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title", ["Independent Director", "Chairman", "Director of Engineering", "Software Engineer",
              "Chief of Staff", "Product Manager"],
)  # fmt: skip
def test_out_of_scope_titles(title):
    assert classify_title(title) is None


def test_founder_and_ceo_gets_both_roles():
    tc = classify_title("CEO & Founder")
    assert tc is not None and tc.seniority == "c_level" and tc.also_founder


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- evidence checks


def test_snippet_must_be_literal_in_source():
    d = doc("https://x.test/a", "Jane Doe is our Chief Technology Officer.\nMore text.")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None, people=[
        person("Jane Doe", "Chief Technology Officer", "Jane Doe is our Chief Technology Officer."),
        person("Jane Doe", "Chief Technology Officer", "Jane Doe leads technology as CTO."),
        person("Jane Doe", "CTO", "Jane Doe is our Chief Technology Officer."),
        person("John Roe", "Chief Executive Officer", "John Roe, CEO of Ramp", works=False),
    ])  # fmt: skip
    claims, rejections = validate(d, ex)
    assert len(claims) == 1
    reasons = [r.reason for r in rejections]
    assert "evidence snippet not found in the source text" in reasons
    assert "title not found in the evidence snippet" in reasons
    assert any(r.startswith("not at the target company") for r in reasons)


def test_whitespace_and_curly_quotes_do_not_break_the_literal_check():
    d = doc("https://x.test/b", "Jane  Doe\nHead of Product at Acme’s HQ")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None, people=[
        person("Jane Doe", "Head of Product", "Jane Doe Head of Product at Acme's HQ"),
    ])  # fmt: skip
    claims, _ = validate(d, ex)
    assert len(claims) == 1


def test_unverified_location_and_date_are_dropped_not_invented():
    d = doc("https://x.test/c", "Jane Doe, VP of Sales, joined last week.")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date="2025-01-01", published_date_snippet="January 1, 2025",
                    people=[person("Jane Doe", "VP of Sales", "Jane Doe, VP of Sales, joined",
                                   location="Denver", location_snippet="based in Denver")])  # fmt: skip
    (claim,), _ = validate(d, ex)
    assert claim.location is None and claim.published_at is None


def test_single_first_name_is_rejected():
    d = doc("https://x.test/d", "Thanks to John, our Head of Sales.")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None,
                    people=[person("John", "Head of Sales", "John, our Head of Sales")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, (rej,) = validate(d, ex)
    assert not claims and isinstance(rej, Rejection) and "full name" in rej.reason


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- currency rules


def test_warnick_former_cfo_in_proxy_is_never_current():
    """The proxy says 'former Chief Financial Officer'; an old newsroom post says CFO."""
    res = resolve_claims(proxy_claims() + news_claims(), today=TODAY)
    warnick = by_name(res, "Jason Warnick")
    assert not warnick.is_current
    assert all(not r.is_current for r in warnick.roles)
    verma = by_name(res, "Shiv Verma")
    assert verma.is_current and verma.confidence == "high"


def test_warnick_from_proxy_alone_is_not_current():
    res = resolve_claims(proxy_claims(), today=TODAY)
    assert not by_name(res, "Jason Warnick").is_current


def test_older_newsroom_c_level_not_in_proxy_is_not_current():
    res = resolve_claims(proxy_claims() + news_claims(), today=TODAY)
    howard = by_name(res, "Gretchen Howard")
    assert not howard.is_current
    assert "proxy" in howard.roles[0].note
    assert any(e["person"] == "Gretchen Howard" for e in res.review["superseded_by_proxy"])


def test_newsroom_c_level_newer_than_proxy_stays_current():
    d = doc("https://robinhood.test/news/2026", "June 2, 2026\nRobinhood names Ann Lee Chief Marketing Officer.")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date="2026-06-02", published_date_snippet="June 2, 2026",
                    people=[person("Ann Lee", "Chief Marketing Officer",
                                   "Robinhood names Ann Lee Chief Marketing Officer.")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, _ = validate(d, ex)
    res = resolve_claims(proxy_claims() + claims, today=TODAY)
    assert by_name(res, "Ann Lee").is_current


def test_vlad_and_vladimir_merge_and_stay_current():
    res = resolve_claims(proxy_claims() + news_claims(), today=TODAY)
    tenev = [p for p in res.people if p.full_name.endswith("Tenev")]
    assert len(tenev) == 1 and tenev[0].is_current
    assert {"names": ["Vlad Tenev", "Vladimir Tenev"]} in res.review["merged_by_nickname_rule"]


def test_uncorroborated_single_source_older_than_18_months_is_low_and_listed():
    d = doc("https://news.test/2023", "May 1, 2023\nAcme hires Bo Park as VP of Data.", "search")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date="2023-05-01", published_date_snippet="May 1, 2023",
                    people=[person("Bo Park", "VP of Data", "Acme hires Bo Park as VP of Data.")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, _ = validate(d, ex)
    res = resolve_claims(claims, today=TODAY)
    park = by_name(res, "Bo Park")
    assert park.is_current and park.confidence == "low"
    assert res.review["stale_single_source"][0]["person"] == "Bo Park"


def test_company_site_role_without_date_is_medium():
    d = doc("https://acme.test/team", "Our team\nBo Park\nHead of Design")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None,
                    people=[person("Bo Park", "Head of Design", "Bo Park Head of Design")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, _ = validate(d, ex)
    assert by_name(resolve_claims(claims, today=TODAY), "Bo Park").confidence == "medium"


def test_blocked_host_records_are_listed_for_review():
    d = doc("https://investors.acme.test/m/bo", "Bo Park, VP of Finance", "search",
            direct_fetch="blocked: investors.acme.test/robots.txt returned HTTP 403")  # fmt: skip
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None,
                    people=[person("Bo Park", "VP of Finance", "Bo Park, VP of Finance")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, _ = validate(d, ex)
    res = resolve_claims(claims, today=TODAY)
    assert res.review["from_blocked_host"] == [
        {"person": "Bo Park", "only_source": True, "urls": ["https://investors.acme.test/m/bo"]}
    ]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- pre-filter


def test_prefilter_keeps_role_lines_and_skips_pages_without_them():
    page = doc("https://x.test/p", "\n".join(["nav"] * 50 + ["Jane Doe", "Head of Product"]))
    text, _ = select_text(page)
    assert "Head of Product" in text and text.count("nav") <= 3
    assert select_text(doc("https://x.test/q", "pricing\nfeatures\ncontact us"))[0] == ""


def test_prefilter_uses_the_sec_executive_officers_span():
    text = "x" * 100 + PROXY_TEXT + "y" * 100
    d = doc("https://sec.test/p", text, "sec_filing", executive_officers_span=[100, 100 + len(PROXY_TEXT)])
    assert select_text(d)[0] == PROXY_TEXT

from pathlib import Path


def sub(path, pairs):
    p = Path(path)
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert s.count(a) == 1, (path, a[:80])
        s = s.replace(a, b)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

        (
            """    # D16 proxy rule: C-level newsroom/search claims older than the latest proxy, for a role
    # the proxy doesn't list for this person, are not current. SEC claims are exempt.
    if (
        is_current
        and seniority == "c_level"
        and proxy_date is not None
        and key not in proxy_keys
        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
        and newest_current < _ordinal(proxy_date)
    ):
        is_current = False
        note = f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim"
""",
            """    # D16 proxy rule: a dated C-level newsroom/search claim older than the latest proxy, for a
    # role the proxy doesn't list for this person, is not current. SEC claims are exempt.
    # Undated claims can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed for review
    # (the proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so e.g. a Chief People Officer may be absent).
    if (
        is_current
        and seniority == "c_level"
        and proxy_date is not None
        and key not in proxy_keys
        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
    ):
        if newest_current <= 0:
            note = f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; source is undated"
        elif newest_current < _ordinal(proxy_date):
            is_current = False
            note = f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim"
""",
        ),
        (
            """    elif "proxy" in r.note:
        review["superseded_by_proxy"].append(entry)""",
            """    elif "source is undated" in r.note:
        review["c_level_not_in_proxy_undated"].append(entry)
    elif "proxy" in r.note:
        review["superseded_by_proxy"].append(entry)""",
        ),
    ],
)

def test_newsroom_c_level_newer_than_proxy_stays_current():''',

cd "/c/Users/pangi/RAG Assignment" && cat >> docs/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

## D16. Currency and confidence rules (Phase 3; proxy and 18-month rules decided by Daniel)

All deterministic, in `pipeline/resolve.py`. The LLM only reports what a page says (`status`: current / former / incoming / unclear).
- **One role per (seniority, function) per person.** The best claim names it: source priority (company_site > sec_filing > search), then newest date.
- **Former wins** unless a current claim for that role is strictly newer (undated counts as oldest). A "former" next to the title in the snippet overrides the model's status. Test: Jason Warnick ("former Chief Financial Officer" in the 2026 proxy) is never current, with or without the 2021 newsroom post.
- **Proxy rule:** for C-level roles, a **dated** newsroom or search claim older than the latest DEF 14A, for a role the proxy doesn't list for that person, is `is_current = false`. SEC claims are exempt. **Undated** claims (e.g. the investors.robinhood.com leadership page) can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed in `c_level_not_in_proxy_undated`. The proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so a Chief People Officer or CISO is normally absent from it. (The first run applied the rule to undated claims too and wrongly retired 7 people. Fixed and tested.)
- **Promotion rule:** an older title is superseded by a later dated title in the same function (Gretchen Howard: VP of Operations in 2018, then COO in 2019). Founder roles are never superseded.
- **Confidence per role:** `high` = an SEC filing, or 2+ sources including the company site. `medium` = the company site, or 2+ sources. `low` = a single search result. **An uncorroborated single-source role last dated more than 18 months ago is `low`** and listed (`stale_single_source`). A person's confidence is that of their best current role.
- **Listed for review, not decided:** two current holders of the same C-level seat (`seat_conflicts`, e.g. Campfire's two CTOs); sources that disagree on currency (`conflicts`); different locations; nickname merges; possible duplicates; records from bot-blocked hosts (D13).
- People with no current role are kept (with their facts), so "who was the CFO before?" can be answered. Lists and counts include only current roles.
- **Rejected:** letting the LLM decide currency or confidence. It doesn't know other sources or the proxy date, and its answer isn't auditable.

## D17. Extraction: structured outputs, cached, pre-filtered

- **Chosen:** `messages.parse(output_format=Extraction)` (Pydantic, `effort=medium`), one call per pre-filtered document, 4 in parallel.
- **Rejected:** tool use with a forced tool choice. `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects forced `tool_choice` (HTTP 400). Structured outputs guarantee the schema without a fake tool. The spec's "tool use + Pydantic" intent (schema-validated output) is unchanged.
- **Pre-filter:** keep ±3 lines around role words (chief, officer, VP, head of, founder, ...) plus date lines. For SEC filings, use the executive-officers section, else the signatures. Pages with no role word skip the LLM. About 12% of documents are skipped.
- **Context:** the prompt names the target company and domain, and asks for the employer plus a `works_at_target_company` flag. That flag rejects customers, partners, and homonymous organizations (campfire.org, robinhood.org).
- **Cache:** responses are cached at `data/<domain>/raw/_extractions/` (gitignored with the rest of the raw data), keyed by model, prompt version, URL and exact input. Re-resolving costs $0. `--reextract` forces new calls. `stats_json` reports both this run's cost and the cost of the cached responses.
- **Refusals / truncation:** a response without structured output is recorded in `extraction_errors` and that document is skipped. No server-side fallback model: a refusal is unlikely on public leadership text, and a silent model switch would muddy cost and provenance.

## D18. Evidence check, with literal re-anchoring

- A claim is kept only if all of these hold: the name appears in the cached source text; the snippet appears literally in it (whitespace, curly quotes and dashes don't count); the snippet contains the last name and the exact title; the title passes the title rules (`titles.py`); the model says the role is held at the target company; and the name has at least two tokens.
- **Re-anchoring:** the model often takes the title from a heading but quotes a sentence that rewords it ("Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations" vs "Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations"). When the exact name and exact title are both in the source within 200 characters, the stored snippet becomes that literal span (`Claim.reanchored`). This cut Robinhood's rejections from 22 to 7 without accepting anything not literally on the page. Rejected: fuzzy snippet matching, which would accept paraphrases.
- Location, bio and page date each need their own verified evidence, or they are dropped (NULL). A rejected claim is kept in `stats_json.rejections` with its reason.
- **Charset fix found here:** SEC filings declare ASCII but contain cp1252 bytes. Decoding them as UTF-8 put `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quote could match. `FetchResult.text_body` now tries the header charset, then UTF-8, then cp1252.

## D19. Schema additions (Phase 3)

- `sources.published_at` (page or filing date, when verified), `facts.is_current` (whether that source presented the title as current), and `roles.as_of` / `roles.note` (newest evidence date; why a role is not current, disputed, or low confidence). All nullable. Missing evidence stays NULL.
- `sources` are rebuilt each run together with people and facts (D3). Only sources that back a stored fact are written.
EOF

cd "/c/Users/pangi/RAG Assignment" && cat >> docs/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

## D20. Fixes from the Phase 3 review

- **Title rule refinement (applies D4):** "C-level" means the company's own C-suite. A title that also carries a VP token is VP-level: "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer" and "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial". So is a subsidiary presidency ("President of Robinhood UK ..."). General Counsel stays C-level, as D4 says, even as "SVP, General Counsel". Company and subsidiary names ("Robinhood Financial") are stripped before a function is assigned, so "Financial" no longer means finance. Without these rules, "how many C-level" was inflated, and there were false seat conflicts (Koller showing up as a second CFO).
- **One document per canonical URL** (lowercase host, no `www.`, no `/us/en` locale prefix, no trailing slash). Discovery keeps the higher-priority copy. Before this, the same newsroom post under two URL spellings counted as two corroborating sources (Zigaitis and Ashkenas were `high`). It also let a role escape the 18-month single-source rule. Robinhood went from 86 to 79 documents.
- A role retired by the proxy rule now reports the dated claims that were retired (title, `as_of`), not an unrelated undated claim.
- Re-anchored evidence (D18) is listed in `review.reanchored` (person, title, URL, snippet), so it can be hand-checked: on a team grid, the nearest title could belong to a neighbour.
- Prices in `extract.py` cite the pricing page and the date they were checked. The client sets `timeout=120s, max_retries=3` explicitly.
EOF

- Pre-filter (role lines, SEC exec-officers span) -> structured-output extraction with

  review lists (conflicts, seat conflicts, stale, blocked host, re-anchored).
- `leadership collect`; writes data/<domain>/leadership.db + leadership.json (committed).
- Charset fix (cp1252 in SEC filings), canonical-URL dedupe, schema: published_at,

"""Full collection run: discover -> pre-filter -> extract (LLM) -> validate -> resolve -> store.

Writes data/<domain>/leadership.db (rebuilt each run, D3) and data/<domain>/leadership.json,
a readable export of the same data. Both are committed; the raw cache is not (D14).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from leadership.config import company_dir, db_path, llm_model
from leadership.pipeline.discover import discover, fetcher_for, normalize_domain, resolve_company
from leadership.pipeline.extract import PROMPT_VERSION, Extractor
from leadership.pipeline.prefilter import select_text
from leadership.pipeline.resolve import Resolution, ResolvedPerson, resolve_claims
from leadership.pipeline.validate import Claim, Rejection, validate
from leadership.sources.base import Company
from leadership.sources.company_site import MAX_PAGES
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import Repository, RoleIn

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class CollectResult:
    company: Company
    resolution: Resolution
    stats: dict[str, Any]
    db_path: Path
    json_path: Path


def collect(
    url: str,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    ticker: str | None = None,
    private: bool = False,
    max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES,
    refresh: bool = False,
    reextract: bool = False,
    today: date | None = None,
) -> CollectResult:
    started = time.monotonic()
    domain = normalize_domain(url)
    with fetcher_for(domain, refresh) as fetcher:
        company = resolve_company(fetcher, url, name, ticker, private)
        found = discover(company, fetcher, max_pages=max_pages)

    jobs, prefilter_skipped = [], []
    for doc in found.documents:
        text, note = select_text(doc)
        if text:
            jobs.append((doc, text))
        else:
            prefilter_skipped.append({"url": doc.url, "reason": note})
    log.info("%d documents, %d sent to the LLM", len(found.documents), len(jobs))

    model = llm_model()
    extractor = Extractor(company, model, company_dir(domain) / "raw" / "_extractions", reextract)
    results, xstats = extractor.extract_all(jobs)

    claims: list[Claim] = []
    rejections: list[Rejection] = []
    for r in results:
        if r.extraction is not None:
            c, rj = validate(r.doc, r.extraction, company.name)
            claims += c
            rejections += rj
    resolution = resolve_claims(claims, today=today)

    stats: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": model,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
        "discovery": found.stats,
        "documents": len(found.documents),
        "documents_sent_to_llm": len(jobs),
        "prefilter_skipped": len(prefilter_skipped),
        "llm_calls": xstats.llm_calls,
        "llm_cached_responses": xstats.cached,
        "tokens_in": xstats.input_tokens,
        "tokens_out": xstats.output_tokens,
        "cost_usd": xstats.cost_usd(model),
        "cost_usd_including_cached": xstats.cost_usd(model, include_cached=True),
        "extraction_errors": xstats.errors,
        "claims_accepted": len(claims),
        "claims_rejected": len(rejections),
        "rejections": [vars(r) for r in rejections],
        "people_found": len(resolution.people),
        "people_current": sum(p.is_current for p in resolution.people),
        "review": resolution.review,
        "duration_s": 0.0,
    }
    path = db_path(domain)
    _store(path, company, resolution, stats, started)
    json_path = export_json(path, domain)
    return CollectResult(company, resolution, stats, path, json_path)


def _store(
    path: Path, company: Company, resolution: Resolution, stats: dict, started: float
) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect(path)
    repo = Repository(conn)
    try:
        with repo.transaction():
            company_id = repo.upsert_company(
                company.name, company.domain, company.is_public, company.ticker
            )
            run_id = repo.start_run(company_id)
            repo.clear_people(company_id)
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM sources WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
            for person in resolution.people:
                _store_person(repo, company_id, person)
            stats["duration_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
            repo.finish_run(run_id, stats)
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _source_id(repo: Repository, company_id: int, claim: Claim, cache: dict[str, int]) -> int:
    doc = claim.doc
    if doc.url not in cache:
        cache[doc.url] = repo.add_source(
            company_id, doc.url, doc.source_type, doc.fetched_at, doc.raw_path, claim.published_at
        )
    return cache[doc.url]


def _store_person(repo: Repository, company_id: int, person: ResolvedPerson) -> None:
    sources: dict[str, int] = {}
    best = next(c for c in person.claims if c.full_name == person.full_name)
    person_id = repo.upsert_person(
        company_id,
        person.full_name,
        _source_id(repo, company_id, best, sources),
        best.evidence_snippet,
    )
    for c in person.claims:
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, c, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "full_name", c.full_name, sid, c.evidence_snippet)
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id, "title", c.title, sid, c.evidence_snippet, is_current=c.status != "former"
        )
    if person.location_claim is not None and person.location_claim.location_snippet:
        lc = person.location_claim
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id,
            "location",
            person.location or "",
            _source_id(repo, company_id, lc, sources),
            lc.location_snippet or "",
        )
    if person.bio_claim is not None and person.bio:
        bc = person.bio_claim
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, bc, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "bio", person.bio, sid, person.bio)
    repo.replace_roles(
        person_id,
        [
            RoleIn(r.title, r.function, r.seniority, r.is_current, r.as_of, r.note or None)
            for r in person.roles
        ],
    )
    repo.update_person_resolved(
        person_id,
        full_name=person.full_name,
        confidence=person.confidence,
        location=person.location,
        bio=person.bio,
        profile_url=person.profile_url,
    )


def export_json(path: Path, domain: str) -> Path:
    """Readable, diff-friendly export of the stored data (committed next to the DB)."""
    conn = connect(path)
    try:
        repo = Repository(conn)
        company = repo.get_company(domain) or {}
        people = repo.all_people(domain)
        run = repo.latest_run(domain)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    out = {"company": company, "latest_run": run, "people": people}
    json_path = path.with_name("leadership.json")
    json_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="
"
    )
    return json_path

Per your rule I kept Tavily's 18 pages at search trust; we never request that host ourselves. Every person sourced from it is listed for your browser check. This is now a general rule (D13): a search result on the company's own domain is dropped if robots.txt explicitly disallows it, and kept but flagged if the host just blocks bots.
- **The raw cache is no longer committed.** `data/*/raw/` is gitignored, and only `leadership.db` and `leadership.json` per company are committed (about 670 KB). Recorded as D14.
- **Campfire's crawl limit is raised:** it now fetches 86 site pages instead of 51 and no longer hits the limit (D15).

**Results.** The live run cost $0.70 per company. LLM responses are cached, so re-running costs $0.

| | Documents | Sent to LLM | Claims kept / rejected | People (current) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Campfire | 113 | 100 | 102 / 0 | 9 (9) |
| Robinhood | 79 | 69 | 127 / 5 | 35 (25) |

**Your Phase 3 rules**

- **18-month rule:** single-source roles last dated more than 18 months ago get low confidence and are listed for review.

**Bugs found and fixed during the phase**
- SEC filings decoded with `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quoted evidence could match. Text now decodes correctly.
- My first version of the proxy rule wrongly retired 7 current people from undated investor-site listings (for example Lucas Moskowitz and Connie Schan). The proxy lists only the officers the SEC requires, so it now applies only to dated claims older than the proxy. Undated ones stay current and are listed for review.
- The same article under two URL spellings counted as corroboration. Duplicates are now merged before counting.
- One commit (a9468cc) contained a broken line in `collect.py`. It was repaired in the next commit (6829634).

**What I'm unsure about, for your review**
1. **Jeff Pinner is not current.** Tavily found an 8-K from 2026-05-07 saying he "would be separating" as CTO, which is newer than the proxy. I believe this is right, but it rests on a search copy of the filing.

"""Full collection run: discover -> pre-filter -> extract (LLM) -> validate -> resolve -> store.

Writes data/<domain>/leadership.db (rebuilt each run, D3) and data/<domain>/leadership.json,
a readable export of the same data. Both are committed; the raw cache is not (D14).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from leadership.config import company_dir, db_path, llm_model
from leadership.pipeline.discover import discover, fetcher_for, normalize_domain, resolve_company
from leadership.pipeline.extract import PROMPT_VERSION, Extractor
from leadership.pipeline.prefilter import select_text
from leadership.pipeline.resolve import Resolution, ResolvedPerson, resolve_claims
from leadership.pipeline.validate import Claim, Rejection, validate
from leadership.sources.base import Company
from leadership.sources.company_site import MAX_PAGES
from leadership.storage.db import connect
from leadership.storage.repository import Repository, RoleIn

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class CollectResult:
    company: Company
    resolution: Resolution
    stats: dict[str, Any]
    db_path: Path
    json_path: Path


def collect(
    url: str,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    ticker: str | None = None,
    private: bool = False,
    max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES,
    refresh: bool = False,
    reextract: bool = False,
    today: date | None = None,
) -> CollectResult:
    started = time.monotonic()
    domain = normalize_domain(url)
    with fetcher_for(domain, refresh) as fetcher:
        company = resolve_company(fetcher, url, name, ticker, private)
        found = discover(company, fetcher, max_pages=max_pages)

    jobs, prefilter_skipped = [], []
    for doc in found.documents:
        text, note = select_text(doc)
        if text:
            jobs.append((doc, text))
        else:
            prefilter_skipped.append({"url": doc.url, "reason": note})
    log.info("%d documents, %d sent to the LLM", len(found.documents), len(jobs))

    model = llm_model()
    extractor = Extractor(company, model, company_dir(domain) / "raw" / "_extractions", reextract)
    results, xstats = extractor.extract_all(jobs)

    claims: list[Claim] = []
    rejections: list[Rejection] = []
    for r in results:
        if r.extraction is not None:
            c, rj = validate(r.doc, r.extraction, company.name)
            claims += c
            rejections += rj
    resolution = resolve_claims(claims, today=today)

    stats: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": model,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
        "discovery": found.stats,
        "documents": len(found.documents),
        "documents_sent_to_llm": len(jobs),
        "prefilter_skipped": len(prefilter_skipped),
        "llm_calls": xstats.llm_calls,
        "llm_cached_responses": xstats.cached,
        "tokens_in": xstats.input_tokens,
        "tokens_out": xstats.output_tokens,
        "cost_usd": xstats.cost_usd(model),
        "cost_usd_including_cached": xstats.cost_usd(model, include_cached=True),
        "extraction_errors": xstats.errors,
        "claims_accepted": len(claims),
        "claims_rejected": len(rejections),
        "rejections": [vars(r) for r in rejections],
        "people_found": len(resolution.people),
        "people_current": sum(p.is_current for p in resolution.people),
        "review": resolution.review,
        "duration_s": 0.0,
    }
    path = db_path(domain)
    _store(path, company, resolution, stats, started)
    json_path = export_json(path, domain)
    return CollectResult(company, resolution, stats, path, json_path)


def _store(
    path: Path, company: Company, resolution: Resolution, stats: dict, started: float
) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect(path)
    repo = Repository(conn)
    try:
        with repo.transaction():
            company_id = repo.upsert_company(
                company.name, company.domain, company.is_public, company.ticker
            )
            run_id = repo.start_run(company_id)
            repo.clear_people(company_id)
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM sources WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
            for person in resolution.people:
                _store_person(repo, company_id, person)
            stats["duration_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
            repo.finish_run(run_id, stats)
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _source_id(repo: Repository, company_id: int, claim: Claim, cache: dict[str, int]) -> int:
    doc = claim.doc
    if doc.url not in cache:
        cache[doc.url] = repo.add_source(
            company_id, doc.url, doc.source_type, doc.fetched_at, doc.raw_path, claim.published_at
        )
    return cache[doc.url]


def _store_person(repo: Repository, company_id: int, person: ResolvedPerson) -> None:
    sources: dict[str, int] = {}
    best = next(c for c in person.claims if c.full_name == person.full_name)
    person_id = repo.upsert_person(
        company_id,
        person.full_name,
        _source_id(repo, company_id, best, sources),
        best.evidence_snippet,
    )
    for c in person.claims:
        sid = _source_id(repo, company_id, c, sources)
        repo.add_fact(person_id, "full_name", c.full_name, sid, c.evidence_snippet)
        repo.add_fact(
            person_id, "title", c.title, sid, c.evidence_snippet, is_current=c.status != "former"
        )

def test_evidence_is_reanchored_to_the_literal_heading_when_the_quote_rewords_the_title():
    text = (
        "Chris Koegel\\nVice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations\\n"
        "Chris Koegel is the Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations."
    )
    d = doc("https://investors.x.test/m/ck", text, "search")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None, people=[
        person("Chris Koegel", "Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations",
               "Chris Koegel is the Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations."),
    ])  # fmt: skip
    (claim,), rejections = validate(d, ex)
    assert not rejections and claim.reanchored
    assert claim.evidence_snippet == (
        "Chris Koegel Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations"
    )


def test_reanchor_handles_table_cells_and_refuses_distant_matches():
    text = "| Date: | May 8, 2026 |\\n| | | | Name: Shiv Verma |\\n| | | | Title: Chief Financial Officer |"
    d = doc("https://sec.test/8k", text, "search")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None, people=[
        person("Shiv Verma", "Chief Financial Officer",
               "Name: Shiv Verma | | | | Title: Chief Financial Officer"),
    ])  # fmt: skip
    (claim,), _ = validate(d, ex)
    assert claim.reanchored and "Shiv Verma" in claim.evidence_snippet

    far = doc("https://x.test/far", "Jane Doe wrote this.\\n" + "filler " * 80 + "\\nHead of Sales")
    ex = Extraction(page_published_date=None, published_date_snippet=None,
                    people=[person("Jane Doe", "Head of Sales", "Jane Doe, Head of Sales")])  # fmt: skip
    claims, (rej,) = validate(far, ex)
    assert not claims and rej.reason == "evidence snippet not found in the source text"


def test_promotion_supersedes_older_title_in_same_function():
    vp = doc("https://rh.test/2018", "November 29, 2018\\nGretchen Howard is joining us as "
             "Vice President of Operations.")  # fmt: skip
    coo = doc("https://rh.test/2019", "June 24, 2019\\nGretchen Howard has been elevated to "
              "Chief Operating Officer.")  # fmt: skip
    claims = []
    for d, title, date_text, iso in [
        (vp, "Vice President of Operations", "November 29, 2018", "2018-11-29"),
        (coo, "Chief Operating Officer", "June 24, 2019", "2019-06-24"),
    ]:
        snippet = d.text.split("\\n", 1)[1]
        ex = Extraction(page_published_date=iso, published_date_snippet=date_text,
                        people=[person("Gretchen Howard", title, snippet)])  # fmt: skip
        claims += validate(d, ex)[0]
    res = resolve_claims(claims, today=TODAY)
    roles = {r.title: r for r in by_name(res, "Gretchen Howard").roles}
    assert not roles["Vice President of Operations"].is_current
    assert "superseded" in roles["Vice President of Operations"].note
    assert roles["Chief Operating Officer"].is_current  # no proxy in this test


def test_plural_shared_titles_classify():
    tc = classify_title("Co-Founders and Co-CEOs")
    assert tc is not None and tc.seniority == "c_level" and tc.also_founder
'''
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("ok")

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, fetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

If you cannot call WebFetch yet and ToolSearch is among your tools, call ToolSearch with `select:WebFetch` first; of the tools it loads, call only the one named exactly `WebFetch`.

**If fetching or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5.5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events. When a streaming request defines user-defined (client) tools, set `eager_input_streaming: true` on each of those tools so large tool inputs (file contents, code, documents) stream as they are generated instead of arriving in one burst after the server finishes buffering them; the client then owns validation: the SDKs' tolerant parsers can return a silently truncated input instead of raising, so validate each parsed tool input against its schema before running it (the typed runner helpers such as `betaZodTool` / typed `@beta_tool` do this; `betaTool()` JSON-Schema tools and manual loops must validate themselves), treat a failure like invalid JSON (`INVALID_JSON` error `tool_result` when you hold the block, re-issue otherwise), check `max_tokens` / `refusal` stop reasons before running tools, and catch only the SDK's JSON error, never its typed API errors - pattern in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming. Leave it off for non-streaming requests, for server tools, and when the request goes through a proxy or an older Bedrock model deployment that rejects the field.

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1/5.2 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Fable and Mythos models, Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, so the sandbox holds only a placeholder unless a service sends the secret back (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |
| Files API / Skills | `client.beta.files.*` / `client.beta.skills.*` with beta `files-api-2025-04-14` / `skills-2025-10-02` | Out of beta: `client.files.*` / `client.skills.*`, no beta header. In current SDKs `client.beta.files` / `client.beta.skills` have breaking shape changes from previous versions, matching the stable namespaces - migrate per `shared/live-sources.md` -> Files API / Skills Guide. |

---

## Subcommands

If the User Request at the bottom of this prompt is a bare subcommand string (no prose), search every **Subcommands** table in this document - including any in sections appended below - and follow the matching Action column directly. This lets users invoke specific flows via `/claude-api <subcommand>`. If no table in the document matches, treat the request as normal prose.

| Subcommand | Action |
