tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

"""SEC EDGAR adapter (public companies only; authoritative for executive officers).

Uses the free official endpoints with the SEC-required User-Agent (SEC_USER_AGENT):
- company_tickers.json to map ticker or name to CIK,
- the submissions API to find the latest 10-K and DEF 14A,
- the filing's primary document from the Archives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import re

from leadership.config import require_setting
from leadership.sources.base import AdapterReport, Company, RawDocument
from leadership.sources.fetch import FetchBlocked, Fetcher, html_to_text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SOURCE_TYPE = "sec_filing"
NAMESPACE = "sec_filing"
TICKERS_URL = "https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json"
SUBMISSIONS_URL = "https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{cik}.json"
ARCHIVE_URL = "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession}/{document}"
FORMS = ("10-K", "DEF 14A")


def _sec_get(fetcher: Fetcher, url: str):
    return fetcher.get(url, NAMESPACE, user_agent=require_setting("SEC_USER_AGENT"))


def _norm(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", "", text.lower()).strip()


def lookup_cik(fetcher: Fetcher, name: str, ticker: str | None) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:
    """Return (cik, ticker, sec_title) or None.

    With a ticker, match it exactly. Without one, accept a name match only if exactly one SEC
    registrant's title starts with the company name as a whole word: a generic name
    ("Campfire") must not latch onto an unrelated registrant. Pass --ticker to be explicit.
    """
    res = _sec_get(fetcher, TICKERS_URL)
    if not res.ok:
        raise RuntimeError(f"SEC ticker list unavailable (HTTP {res.status})")
    rows = json.loads(res.text_body()).values()
    if ticker:
        hits = [r for r in rows if r["ticker"].upper() == ticker.upper()]
    else:
        key = _norm(name)
        hits = [r for r in rows if re.match(rf"{re.escape(key)}\b", _norm(r["title"]))]
        if len({r["cik_str"] for r in hits}) != 1:
            if hits:
                titles = sorted({r["title"] for r in hits})[:5]
                log.info("SEC name match for %r is ambiguous (%s); private", name, titles)
            return None
    if not hits:
        return None
    row = hits[0]
    return str(row["cik_str"]).zfill(10), row["ticker"], row["title"]


EXEC_HEADING = (
    r"^(information about (our )?)?executive officers( of the registrant| of the company)?\.?$"
)


def find_section(text: str, heading_pattern: str = EXEC_HEADING, max_len: int = 20_000):
    """Character span of the executive-officers section, or None.

    Headings appear several times (table of contents, page headers, exhibit index), so pick
    the heading followed by the most title lines (lines ending in "Officer") before the next
    heading or 3,000 characters. Only a hint for pre-filtering: extraction still sees, and
    is checked against, the full text.
    """
    matches = list(re.finditer(heading_pattern, text, flags=re.I | re.M))
    best: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        end = m.end() + 3000
        if i + 1 < len(matches):
            end = min(end, matches[i + 1].start())
        score = len(re.findall(r"\bOfficer,?$", text[m.end() : end], flags=re.M))
        if score and (best is None or score >= best[1]):  # ties: later wins (body after TOC)
            best = (m.start(), score)
    if best is None:
        return None
    return best[0], min(len(text), best[0] + max_len)


class SecEdgarAdapter:
    source_type = SOURCE_TYPE

    def __init__(self, fetcher: Fetcher) -> None:
        self.fetcher = fetcher

    def discover(self, company: Company) -> AdapterReport:
        report = AdapterReport(SOURCE_TYPE)
        if not company.is_public or not company.cik:
            report.notes.append("not a public company (no SEC registrant matched); skipped")
            return report
        url = SUBMISSIONS_URL.format(cik=company.cik)
        try:
            sub = _sec_get(self.fetcher, url)
        except FetchBlocked as exc:
            report.skip(url, str(exc))
            return report
        if not sub.ok:
            report.skip(url, f"HTTP {sub.status}")
            return report
        recent = json.loads(sub.text_body())["filings"]["recent"]
        latest: dict[str, int] = {}
        for i, form in enumerate(recent["form"]):
            if form in FORMS and form not in latest:
                latest[form] = i  # `recent` is newest first
        for form in FORMS:
            if form not in latest:
                report.notes.append(f"no {form} in recent filings")
                continue
            i = latest[form]
            doc_url = ARCHIVE_URL.format(
                cik=int(company.cik),
                accession=recent["accessionNumber"][i].replace("-", ""),
                document=recent["primaryDocument"][i],
            )
            try:
                res = _sec_get(self.fetcher, doc_url)
            except FetchBlocked as exc:
                report.skip(doc_url, str(exc))
                continue
            if not res.ok:
                report.skip(doc_url, f"HTTP {res.status}")
                continue
            text, _ = html_to_text(res.text_body())
            raw_path = self.fetcher.write_text(NAMESPACE, doc_url, text)
            span = find_section(text)
            if span is None:
                report.notes.append(f"{form}: no executive officers section found")
            report.documents.append(
                RawDocument(
                    url=doc_url,
                    source_type=SOURCE_TYPE,
                    title=f"{company.name} {form} filed {recent['filingDate'][i]}",
                    text=text,
                    fetched_at=res.fetched_at,
                    raw_path=raw_path,
                    meta={
                        "form": form,
                        "filing_date": recent["filingDate"][i],
                        "report_date": recent["reportDate"][i],
                        "executive_officers_span": span,
                    },
                )
            )
        return report
"""Shared types for source adapters."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Protocol


@dataclass
class Company:
    name: str  # display name used in search queries, e.g. "Robinhood"
    domain: str  # the input domain; names the data folder, e.g. "meetcampfire.com"
    site_url: str  # where the site actually lives after redirects, e.g. "https://campfire.ai/"
    is_public: bool = False
    ticker: str | None = None
    cik: str | None = None  # SEC Central Index Key, zero-padded to 10 digits


@dataclass
class RawDocument:
    url: str
    source_type: str  # company_site | sec_filing | search
    title: str
    text: str  # plain text; evidence snippets are checked against exactly this
    fetched_at: str
    raw_path: str  # repo-relative path of the cached text file (`text` above)
    meta: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class AdapterReport:
    """What an adapter tried, so empty or blocked sources are visible, never silent."""

    source_type: str
    documents: list[RawDocument] = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # {"url", "reason"}
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def skip(self, url: str, reason: str) -> None:
        self.skipped.append({"url": url, "reason": reason})


class SourceAdapter(Protocol):
    source_type: str

    def discover(self, company: Company) -> AdapterReport: ...

"""SEC EDGAR adapter (public companies only; authoritative for executive officers).

Uses the free official endpoints with the SEC-required User-Agent (SEC_USER_AGENT):
- company_tickers.json to map ticker or name to CIK,
- the submissions API to find the latest 10-K and DEF 14A,
- the filing's primary document from the Archives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import re

from leadership.config import require_setting
from leadership.sources.base import AdapterReport, Company, RawDocument
from leadership.sources.fetch import FetchBlocked, Fetcher, html_to_text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SOURCE_TYPE = "sec_filing"
NAMESPACE = "sec_filing"
TICKERS_URL = "https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json"
SUBMISSIONS_URL = "https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{cik}.json"
ARCHIVE_URL = "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession}/{document}"
FORMS = ("10-K", "DEF 14A")


def _sec_get(fetcher: Fetcher, url: str):
    return fetcher.get(url, NAMESPACE, user_agent=require_setting("SEC_USER_AGENT"))


def _norm(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", "", text.lower()).strip()


def lookup_cik(fetcher: Fetcher, name: str, ticker: str | None) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:
    """Return (cik, ticker, sec_title) or None.

    With a ticker, match it exactly. Without one, accept a name match only if exactly one SEC
    registrant's title starts with the company name as a whole word: a generic name
    ("Campfire") must not latch onto an unrelated registrant. Pass --ticker to be explicit.
    """
    res = _sec_get(fetcher, TICKERS_URL)
    if not res.ok:
        raise RuntimeError(f"SEC ticker list unavailable (HTTP {res.status})")
    rows = json.loads(res.text_body()).values()
    if ticker:
        hits = [r for r in rows if r["ticker"].upper() == ticker.upper()]
    else:
        key = _norm(name)
        hits = [r for r in rows if re.match(rf"{re.escape(key)}\b", _norm(r["title"]))]
        if len({r["cik_str"] for r in hits}) != 1:
            if hits:
                titles = sorted({r["title"] for r in hits})[:5]
                log.info("SEC name match for %r is ambiguous (%s); private", name, titles)
            return None
    if not hits:
        return None
    row = hits[0]
    return str(row["cik_str"]).zfill(10), row["ticker"], row["title"]


EXEC_HEADING = (
    r"^(information about (our )?)?executive officers( of the registrant| of the company)?\.?$"
)


def find_section(text: str, heading_pattern: str = EXEC_HEADING, max_len: int = 20_000):
    """Character span of the executive-officers section, or None.

    Headings appear several times (table of contents, page headers, exhibit index), so pick
    the heading followed by the most title lines (lines ending in "Officer") before the next
    heading or 3,000 characters. Only a hint for pre-filtering: extraction still sees, and
    is checked against, the full text.
    """
    matches = list(re.finditer(heading_pattern, text, flags=re.I | re.M))
    best: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        end = m.end() + 3000
        if i + 1 < len(matches):
            end = min(end, matches[i + 1].start())
        score = len(re.findall(r"\bOfficer,?$", text[m.end() : end], flags=re.M))
        if score and (best is None or score >= best[1]):  # ties: later wins (body after TOC)
            best = (m.start(), score)
    if best is None:
        return None
    return best[0], min(len(text), best[0] + max_len)


class SecEdgarAdapter:
    source_type = SOURCE_TYPE

    def __init__(self, fetcher: Fetcher) -> None:
        self.fetcher = fetcher

    def discover(self, company: Company) -> AdapterReport:
        report = AdapterReport(SOURCE_TYPE)
        if not company.is_public or not company.cik:
            report.notes.append("not a public company (no SEC registrant matched); skipped")
            return report
        url = SUBMISSIONS_URL.format(cik=company.cik)
        try:
            sub = _sec_get(self.fetcher, url)
        except FetchBlocked as exc:
            report.skip(url, str(exc))
            return report
        if not sub.ok:
            report.skip(url, f"HTTP {sub.status}")
            return report
        recent = json.loads(sub.text_body())["filings"]["recent"]
        latest: dict[str, int] = {}
        for i, form in enumerate(recent["form"]):
            if form in FORMS and form not in latest:
                latest[form] = i  # `recent` is newest first
        for form in FORMS:
            if form not in latest:
                report.notes.append(f"no {form} in recent filings")
                continue
            i = latest[form]
            doc_url = ARCHIVE_URL.format(
                cik=int(company.cik),
                accession=recent["accessionNumber"][i].replace("-", ""),
                document=recent["primaryDocument"][i],
            )
            try:
                res = _sec_get(self.fetcher, doc_url)
            except FetchBlocked as exc:
                report.skip(doc_url, str(exc))
                continue
            if not res.ok:
                report.skip(doc_url, f"HTTP {res.status}")
                continue
            text, _ = html_to_text(res.text_body())
            raw_path = self.fetcher.write_text(NAMESPACE, doc_url, text)
            span = find_section(text)
            if span is None:
                report.notes.append(f"{form}: no executive officers section found")
            report.documents.append(
                RawDocument(
                    url=doc_url,
                    source_type=SOURCE_TYPE,
                    title=f"{company.name} {form} filed {recent['filingDate'][i]}",
                    text=text,
                    fetched_at=res.fetched_at,
                    raw_path=raw_path,
                    meta={
                        "form": form,
                        "filing_date": recent["filingDate"][i],
                        "report_date": recent["reportDate"][i],
                        "executive_officers_span": span,
                    },
                )
            )
        return report

"""Keyword pre-filter (no LLM): which parts of a document are worth sending to the model.

Pages are long (nav, footers, product copy); leaders appear in a few lines. We keep windows of
lines around leadership keywords and skip documents with no hit at all, so the LLM sees less
text and costs less. The evidence check (validate.py) still runs against the *full* text.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from leadership.sources.base import RawDocument

# A line that mentions a leadership role ("Head of Product", "names Jane Doe CFO").
ROLE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:chief|officer|ceo|cfo|cto|coo|president|vice president|vp|head of|founder|counsel)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# Publication dates ("March 3, 2025", "2025-03-03"), so the model can report the page date.
DATE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s+\d{1,2},?\s+(?:19|20)\d\d\b"
    r"|\b(?:19|20)\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
MAX_DATE_LINES = 3
WINDOW_LINES = 3
MAX_CHARS = 24_000  # per document sent to the model; the rest is dropped with a note


def select_text(doc: RawDocument) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(text for the model, note). Empty text means: no leadership signal, skip the LLM."""
    text = doc.text
    if doc.source_type == "sec_filing":
        span = doc.meta.get("executive_officers_span")
        if span:
            return text[span[0] : span[1]], "SEC executive officers section"
        sig = text.rfind("SIGNATURES")
        if sig >= 0:
            return text[sig : sig + MAX_CHARS], "SEC signatures section"
        return "", "SEC filing without an executive officers or signatures section"

    lines = text.splitlines()
    keep: set[int] = set()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if ROLE_LINE.search(line):
            keep.update(range(max(0, i - WINDOW_LINES), min(len(lines), i + WINDOW_LINES + 1)))
    if not keep:
        return "", "no leadership keywords"
    dates = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if DATE_LINE.search(line)][:MAX_DATE_LINES]
    keep.update(dates)

    chunks: list[str] = []
    prev = -2
    for i in sorted(keep):
        if i != prev + 1 and chunks:
            chunks.append("[...]")
        chunks.append(lines[i])
        prev = i
    selected = "\n".join(chunks)
    note = f"{len(keep)} of {len(lines)} lines"
    if len(selected) > MAX_CHARS:
        selected = selected[:MAX_CHARS]
        note += f", truncated to {MAX_CHARS} chars"
    return selected, note
    cached_input_tokens: int = 0  # what the cached responses cost when they were made
    cached_output_tokens: int = 0
    errors: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)

    def cost_usd(self, model: str, include_cached: bool = False) -> float | None:
        price = PRICES.get(model)
        if price is None:
            return None
        tin, tout = self.input_tokens, self.output_tokens
        if include_cached:
            tin, tout = tin + self.cached_input_tokens, tout + self.cached_output_tokens
        return round((tin * price[0] + tout * price[1]) / 1e6, 4)


def _user_prompt(doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> str:
    meta_date = doc.meta.get("published_date") or doc.meta.get("filing_date") or "unknown"
    return (
        f"Source URL: {doc.url}\nPage title: {doc.title}\n"
        f"Publication date from metadata (may be missing): {meta_date}\n\n"
        f"<page>\n{text}\n</page>"
    )


class Extractor:
    def __init__(self, company: Company, model: str, cache_dir: Path, reextract: bool = False):
        self.company = company
        self.model = model
        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
        self.reextract = reextract
        self.system = SYSTEM.format(name=company.name, domain=company.domain)
        self._client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None

    def _client_lazy(self) -> anthropic.Anthropic:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(
                api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"), timeout=120.0, max_retries=3
            )
        return self._client

    def _cache_path(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> Path:
        key = hashlib.sha256(
            "\x00".join([self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self.system, doc.url, text]).encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()[:24]
        return self.cache_dir / f"{key}.json"

    def extract(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> ExtractResult:
        path = self._cache_path(doc, text)
        if path.exists() and not self.reextract:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            usage = data.get("usage", {})
            return ExtractResult(
                doc,
                Extraction.model_validate(data["extraction"]),
                usage.get("input_tokens", 0),
                usage.get("output_tokens", 0),
                from_cache=True,
            )
        try:
            response = self._client_lazy().messages.parse(
                model=self.model,
                max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
                system=self.system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": _user_prompt(doc, text)}],
                output_format=Extraction,
                output_config={"effort": EFFORT},
            )
        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
        except anthropic.APIError as exc:
            log.warning("extraction failed for %s: %s", doc.url, exc)
            return ExtractResult(doc, None, error=f"API error: {exc}")
        usage = response.usage
        result = ExtractResult(doc, None, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens)
        if response.stop_reason in ("refusal", "max_tokens") or response.parsed_output is None:
            result.error = f"no structured output (stop_reason={response.stop_reason})"
            return result
        result.extraction = response.parsed_output
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            "url": doc.url,
            "model": self.model,
            "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
            "usage": {"input_tokens": usage.input_tokens, "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens},
            "extraction": result.extraction.model_dump(),
        }
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        return result

    def extract_all(
        self, jobs: list[tuple[RawDocument, str]]
    ) -> tuple[list[ExtractResult], ExtractStats]:
        stats = ExtractStats()
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda job: self.extract(*job), jobs))
        for r in results:
            if r.from_cache:
                stats.cached += 1
                stats.cached_input_tokens += r.input_tokens
                stats.cached_output_tokens += r.output_tokens
            else:
                stats.llm_calls += 1
                stats.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
                stats.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
            if r.error:
                stats.errors.append({"url": r.doc.url, "error": r.error})
        return results, stats

_BLOCK_TAGS = frozenset(
    "address article aside blockquote body br caption dd details dialog div dl dt fieldset "
    "figcaption figure footer form h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 header hr li main nav ol p pre section "
    "summary table tbody td tfoot th thead tr ul".split()
)


def html_blocks(html: str) -> list[str]:
    """Text of each innermost block element, inline children joined with spaces.

    Used only to re-anchor evidence (validate.py): a name and a title count as one statement
    only if they sit in the same block, so a team grid can't pair a name with a neighbour's
    title. doc.text (what the LLM sees and evidence is checked against) is not changed.
    """
    tree = HTMLParser(html)
    tree.strip_tags(list(_DROP_TAGS))
    root = tree.body or tree.root
    blocks: list[str] = []
    buf: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        text = " ".join(" ".join(buf).split())
        if text:
            blocks.append(text)
        buf.clear()

    def walk(node) -> None:
        for child in node.iter(include_text=True):
            if child.tag == "-text":
                buf.append(child.text_content or "")
            elif child.tag in _BLOCK_TAGS:
                flush()
                walk(child)
                flush()
            else:
                walk(child)

    if root is not None:
        walk(root)
        flush()
    return blocks


class Fetcher:

29:## D4. Schema details (reviewed with Daniel in Phase 0)
30-
31-- **Source priority is derived, not stored.** `SOURCE_PRIORITY` in `models.py` maps `sources.source_type` to a priority: company_site (0) beats sec_filing (1), which beats search (2). Rejected: a `facts.source_priority` column, which would duplicate `source_type` and could drift from it.
32-- **`source_count` is computed in the query** (distinct `source_id` across the person's facts). Rejected: storing it on `roles`, where it could go stale after a re-resolve.
33-- **No `exec` seniority.** President and General Counsel map to `c_level`, because the 10-K lists them as executive officers. `title_raw` always keeps the original title, so nothing is lost. Allowed seniorities: `c_level | vp | head | founder`.
34-- **Dedupe key:** `people` is unique on `(company_id, normalized_name)`. `normalize_name` strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics and suffixes, and middle initials. It deliberately does **not** merge nicknames ("Vlad" vs "Vladimir"). A wrong merge would combine two people's facts, which is worse than a duplicate that shows up in validation.
35-- **`facts.field`** is restricted to `full_name | title | location | bio`.
36-- **`collection_runs.stats_json`** holds tokens in and out, cost, document counts per source, people found, and rejected extractions with reasons.
37-- **Counts are of people, not roles.** A CEO who is also a co-founder counts once in "how many leaders".
38-
39-## D5. Configuration via environment
40-
41-- `.env` at the repo root is loaded automatically (`python-dotenv`). Variables: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `SEC_USER_AGENT` (used as-is, e.g. `"Jane Doe jane@example.com"`, as SEC requires), and `LLM_MODEL` (blank means `claude-sonnet-5-5`).
42-- Only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is needed to run chat, eval, and the UI against the committed data. `TAVILY_API_KEY` and `SEC_USER_AGENT` are only needed for `leadership collect`. A missing key raises an error that names the variable and says where to get it.
43-
--
46:- **Problem:** The same person appears under different first names across sources. Robinhood's site likely says "Vlad Tenev" while the SEC filings say "Vladimir Tenev". Exact normalized-name matching (D4) would create two people.
47-- **Chosen:** `compare_identity` in `pipeline/resolve.py` merges two records (SAME) only when **all** of these hold:
48-  - same company;
49-  - same last name;
50-  - the first names match: identical, one is a prefix of the other (shorter one at least 3 letters, e.g. Vlad/Vladimir), or both are in a small, explicit nickname map (Bob/Robert, Bill/William, ...);
51-  - at least one overlapping role `function`.
52-- **Close but not merged** is returned as POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE and listed in `VALIDATION.md` for Daniel to decide. This covers: same last name with matching first names but no overlapping function; same last name and same first initial; same first initial and last names at least 0.8 similar (e.g. Steven Quirk / Stephen Quirke); or whole-name similarity of 0.85 or higher.
53-- **Every non-exact merge is also listed** in `VALIDATION.md` ("merged by nickname rule"), so a wrong merge is visible.
54-- **Accepted risk:** The prefix rule merges "Chris Lee" and "Christine Lee" if their functions overlap. A test documents this case. The reviewer-visible merge list is the mitigation.
55-- **Rejected:** fuzzy matching (edit distance) as the merge criterion, which risks silently mixing two people's facts. Also rejected: an LLM judging identity, which is non-deterministic and hard to audit. Also rejected: a large nickname database, which goes beyond what two test companies need.
56-
57-## D7. Tavily as the one web search API
58-
59-- **Chosen:** Tavily (`search_depth=basic`, 8 results, `include_raw_content=text`), with 10 targeted queries per company (CEO, CTO, CFO, "chief" officer, VP, "vice president", "head of", appoints/hires/names, leadership team, founder).
- **Rejected:** letting the LLM decide currency or confidence. It doesn't know other sources or the proxy date, and its answer isn't auditable.

## D17. Extraction: structured outputs, cached, pre-filtered

- **Chosen:** `messages.parse(output_format=Extraction)` (Pydantic, `effort=medium`), one call per pre-filtered document, 4 in parallel.
- **Rejected:** tool use with a forced tool choice. `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects forced `tool_choice` (HTTP 400). Structured outputs guarantee the schema without a fake tool. The spec's "tool use + Pydantic" intent (schema-validated output) is unchanged.
- **Pre-filter:** keep ±3 lines around role words (chief, officer, VP, head of, founder, ...) plus date lines. For SEC filings, use the executive-officers section, else the signatures. Pages with no role word skip the LLM. About 12% of documents are skipped.
- **Context:** the prompt names the target company and domain, and asks for the employer plus a `works_at_target_company` flag. That flag rejects customers, partners, and homonymous organizations (campfire.org, robinhood.org).
- **Cache:** responses are cached at `data/<domain>/raw/_extractions/` (gitignored with the rest of the raw data), keyed by model, prompt version, URL and exact input. Re-resolving costs $0. `--reextract` forces new calls. `stats_json` reports both this run's cost and the cost of the cached responses.
- **Refusals / truncation:** a response without structured output is recorded in `extraction_errors` and that document is skipped. No server-side fallback model: a refusal is unlikely on public leadership text, and a silent model switch would muddy cost and provenance.

## D18. Evidence check, with literal re-anchoring

- A claim is kept only if all of these hold: the name appears in the cached source text; the snippet appears literally in it (whitespace, curly quotes and dashes don't count); the snippet contains the last name and the exact title; the title passes the title rules (`titles.py`); the model says the role is held at the target company; and the name has at least two tokens.
- **Re-anchoring:** the model often takes the title from a heading but quotes a sentence that rewords it ("Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations" vs "Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations"). When the exact name and exact title are both in the source within 200 characters, the stored snippet becomes that literal span (`Claim.reanchored`). This cut Robinhood's rejections from 22 to 7 without accepting anything not literally on the page. Rejected: fuzzy snippet matching, which would accept paraphrases.
- Location, bio and page date each need their own verified evidence, or they are dropped (NULL). A rejected claim is kept in `stats_json.rejections` with its reason.
- **Charset fix found here:** SEC filings declare ASCII but contain cp1252 bytes. Decoding them as UTF-8 put `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quote could match. `FetchResult.text_body` now tries the header charset, then UTF-8, then cp1252.

## D19. Schema additions (Phase 3)

- `sources.published_at` (page or filing date, when verified), `facts.is_current` (whether that source presented the title as current), and `roles.as_of` / `roles.note` (newest evidence date; why a role is not current, disputed, or low confidence). All nullable. Missing evidence stays NULL.
- `sources` are rebuilt each run together with people and facts (D3). Only sources that back a stored fact are written.

## D20. Fixes from the Phase 3 review

- **Title rule refinement (applies D4):** "C-level" means the company's own C-suite. A title that also carries a VP token is VP-level: "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer" and "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial". So is a subsidiary presidency ("President of Robinhood UK ..."). General Counsel stays C-level, as D4 says, even as "SVP, General Counsel". Company and subsidiary names ("Robinhood Financial") are stripped before a function is assigned, so "Financial" no longer means finance. Without these rules, "how many C-level" was inflated, and there were false seat conflicts (Koller showing up as a second CFO).
- **One document per canonical URL** (lowercase host, no `www.`, no `/us/en` locale prefix, no trailing slash). Discovery keeps the higher-priority copy. Before this, the same newsroom post under two URL spellings counted as two corroborating sources (Zigaitis and Ashkenas were `high`). It also let a role escape the 18-month single-source rule. Robinhood went from 86 to 79 documents.
- A role retired by the proxy rule now reports the dated claims that were retired (title, `as_of`), not an unrelated undated claim.
- Re-anchored evidence (D18) is listed in `review.reanchored` (person, title, URL, snippet), so it can be hand-checked: on a team grid, the nearest title could belong to a neighbour.

30-
31-- **Source priority is derived, not stored.** `SOURCE_PRIORITY` in `models.py` maps `sources.source_type` to a priority: company_site (0) beats sec_filing (1), which beats search (2). Rejected: a `facts.source_priority` column, which would duplicate `source_type` and could drift from it.
32-- **`source_count` is computed in the query** (distinct `source_id` across the person's facts). Rejected: storing it on `roles`, where it could go stale after a re-resolve.
33-- **No `exec` seniority.** President and General Counsel map to `c_level`, because the 10-K lists them as executive officers. `title_raw` always keeps the original title, so nothing is lost. Allowed seniorities: `c_level | vp | head | founder`.
34-- **Dedupe key:** `people` is unique on `(company_id, normalized_name)`. `normalize_name` strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics and suffixes, and middle initials. It deliberately does **not** merge nicknames ("Vlad" vs "Vladimir"). A wrong merge would combine two people's facts, which is worse than a duplicate that shows up in validation.
35-- **`facts.field`** is restricted to `full_name | title | location | bio`.
36-- **`collection_runs.stats_json`** holds tokens in and out, cost, document counts per source, people found, and rejected extractions with reasons.
37-- **Counts are of people, not roles.** A CEO who is also a co-founder counts once in "how many leaders".
38-
39-## D5. Configuration via environment
40-
41-- `.env` at the repo root is loaded automatically (`python-dotenv`). Variables: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `SEC_USER_AGENT` (used as-is, e.g. `"Jane Doe jane@example.com"`, as SEC requires), and `LLM_MODEL` (blank means `claude-sonnet-5-5`).
42-- Only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is needed to run chat, eval, and the UI against the committed data. `TAVILY_API_KEY` and `SEC_USER_AGENT` are only needed for `leadership collect`. A missing key raises an error that names the variable and says where to get it.
43-
--
46:- **Problem:** The same person appears under different first names across sources. Robinhood's site likely says "Vlad Tenev" while the SEC filings say "Vladimir Tenev". Exact normalized-name matching (D4) would create two people.
47-- **Chosen:** `compare_identity` in `pipeline/resolve.py` merges two records (SAME) only when **all** of these hold:
48-  - same company;
49-  - same last name;
50-  - the first names match: identical, one is a prefix of the other (shorter one at least 3 letters, e.g. Vlad/Vladimir), or both are in a small, explicit nickname map (Bob/Robert, Bill/William, ...);
51-  - at least one overlapping role `function`.
52-- **Close but not merged** is returned as POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE and listed in `VALIDATION.md` for Daniel to decide. This covers: same last name with matching first names but no overlapping function; same last name and same first initial; same first initial and last names at least 0.8 similar (e.g. Steven Quirk / Stephen Quirke); or whole-name similarity of 0.85 or higher.
53-- **Every non-exact merge is also listed** in `VALIDATION.md` ("merged by nickname rule"), so a wrong merge is visible.
54-- **Accepted risk:** The prefix rule merges "Chris Lee" and "Christine Lee" if their functions overlap. A test documents this case. The reviewer-visible merge list is the mitigation.
55-- **Rejected:** fuzzy matching (edit distance) as the merge criterion, which risks silently mixing two people's facts. Also rejected: an LLM judging identity, which is non-deterministic and hard to audit. Also rejected: a large nickname database, which goes beyond what two test companies need.
56-
57-## D7. Tavily as the one web search API
58-
59-- **Chosen:** Tavily (`search_depth=basic`, 8 results, `include_raw_content=text`), with 10 targeted queries per company (CEO, CTO, CFO, "chief" officer, VP, "vice president", "head of", appoints/hires/names, leadership team, founder).
- **Rejected:** letting the LLM decide currency or confidence. It doesn't know other sources or the proxy date, and its answer isn't auditable.

## D17. Extraction: structured outputs, cached, pre-filtered

- **Chosen:** `messages.parse(output_format=Extraction)` (Pydantic, `effort=medium`), one call per pre-filtered document, 4 in parallel.
- **Rejected:** tool use with a forced tool choice. `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects forced `tool_choice` (HTTP 400). Structured outputs guarantee the schema without a fake tool. The spec's "tool use + Pydantic" intent (schema-validated output) is unchanged.
- **Pre-filter:** keep ±3 lines around role words (chief, officer, VP, head of, founder, ...) plus date lines. For SEC filings, use the executive-officers section, else the signatures. Pages with no role word skip the LLM. About 12% of documents are skipped.
- **Context:** the prompt names the target company and domain, and asks for the employer plus a `works_at_target_company` flag. That flag rejects customers, partners, and homonymous organizations (campfire.org, robinhood.org).
- **Cache:** responses are cached at `data/<domain>/raw/_extractions/` (gitignored with the rest of the raw data), keyed by model, prompt version, URL and exact input. Re-resolving costs $0. `--reextract` forces new calls. `stats_json` reports both this run's cost and the cost of the cached responses.
- **Refusals / truncation:** a response without structured output is recorded in `extraction_errors` and that document is skipped. No server-side fallback model: a refusal is unlikely on public leadership text, and a silent model switch would muddy cost and provenance.

## D18. Evidence check, with literal re-anchoring

- A claim is kept only if all of these hold: the name appears in the cached source text; the snippet appears literally in it (whitespace, curly quotes and dashes don't count); the snippet contains the last name and the exact title; the title passes the title rules (`titles.py`); the model says the role is held at the target company; and the name has at least two tokens.
- **Re-anchoring:** the model often takes the title from a heading but quotes a sentence that rewords it ("Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations" vs "Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations"). When the exact name and exact title are both in the source within 200 characters, the stored snippet becomes that literal span (`Claim.reanchored`). This cut Robinhood's rejections from 22 to 7 without accepting anything not literally on the page. Rejected: fuzzy snippet matching, which would accept paraphrases.
- Location, bio and page date each need their own verified evidence, or they are dropped (NULL). A rejected claim is kept in `stats_json.rejections` with its reason.
- **Charset fix found here:** SEC filings declare ASCII but contain cp1252 bytes. Decoding them as UTF-8 put `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quote could match. `FetchResult.text_body` now tries the header charset, then UTF-8, then cp1252.

## D19. Schema additions (Phase 3)

- `sources.published_at` (page or filing date, when verified), `facts.is_current` (whether that source presented the title as current), and `roles.as_of` / `roles.note` (newest evidence date; why a role is not current, disputed, or low confidence). All nullable. Missing evidence stays NULL.
- `sources` are rebuilt each run together with people and facts (D3). Only sources that back a stored fact are written.

## D20. Fixes from the Phase 3 review

- **Title rule refinement (applies D4):** "C-level" means the company's own C-suite. A title that also carries a VP token is VP-level: "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer" and "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial". So is a subsidiary presidency ("President of Robinhood UK ..."). General Counsel stays C-level, as D4 says, even as "SVP, General Counsel". Company and subsidiary names ("Robinhood Financial") are stripped before a function is assigned, so "Financial" no longer means finance. Without these rules, "how many C-level" was inflated, and there were false seat conflicts (Koller showing up as a second CFO).
- **One document per canonical URL** (lowercase host, no `www.`, no `/us/en` locale prefix, no trailing slash). Discovery keeps the higher-priority copy. Before this, the same newsroom post under two URL spellings counted as two corroborating sources (Zigaitis and Ashkenas were `high`). It also let a role escape the 18-month single-source rule. Robinhood went from 86 to 79 documents.
- A role retired by the proxy rule now reports the dated claims that were retired (title, `as_of`), not an unrelated undated claim.
- Re-anchored evidence (D18) is listed in `review.reanchored` (person, title, URL, snippet), so it can be hand-checked: on a team grid, the nearest title could belong to a neighbour.
- Prices in `extract.py` cite the pricing page and the date they were checked. The client sets `timeout=120s, max_retries=3` explicitly.

A second 8-K, from 2026-06-26, added a new person: Dara Bazzano, Chief Accounting Officer.
2. **Campfire's two CTOs stay undecided:** Paul Nichols (2026) and Fernando San Martin (2024, low confidence) are both still listed as a seat conflict.

   - Alexandra Roveda stays, because her evidence reads "Campfire appointed Alexandra Roveda…". A name match can't tell two companies called Campfire apart, so she stays on the hand-check list.

Robinhood lost some claims from one-person investor profile pages, but no people, since each person also appears on one line of the investor-site leadership page.

== .claude/agents/coverage-scout.md
---
name: coverage-scout
description: Builds an independent, blind list of a company's leadership from public web sources, so it can be compared against the pipeline's output to measure recall. Use PROACTIVELY in phase 4, before the pipeline's results are reviewed. It must never see the pipeline's data.
tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, Write
model: sonnet
---

You are an independent research analyst. Your job is to build, **from scratch and blind**, the best list you can of a company's current leadership. Your list is the answer key used to find people the automated pipeline missed. You deliberately have no access to the repo's code or data. Don't ask for it, and don't try to infer it.

## Scope

- **Leadership** means: C-level (CEO, CTO, CFO, COO, CMO, CPO, CISO, CLO/General Counsel, CHRO/CPO-People, etc.), all VP levels (VP, SVP, EVP), Heads of departments, and founders still in an operating role.
- **Excluded:** board-only members, advisors, investors, former employees, and managers below Head level.

## Hard rules

- **No LinkedIn.** Don't fetch linkedin.com, and ignore LinkedIn search results entirely. The project excludes it as a source, so your answer key must play by the same rules or the comparison is unfair.
- Don't fetch sites whose ToS forbids automated access. Respect obvious paywalls.
- **Every person needs a URL** that you actually fetched and read, showing their name and title. A search snippet alone isn't enough. Search snippets can be stale or wrong.
- Prefer current information. Note the publication date of each source. Mark anything older than 18 months as `possibly stale`.
- Budget: about 25 searches and about 30 fetches per company. Stop when new searches stop turning up new people.

## Search strategy (in order)

1. The company's own site: `/about`, `/team`, `/leadership`, `/company`, the newsroom or press pages.
2. For public companies: the SEC EDGAR latest 10-K "Information about our Executive Officers" and the DEF 14A proxy.
3. Press releases and news, such as `"<company>" appoints`, `"<company>" names * as`, `"<company>" "VP of"`, `"<company>" "Head of"`, and `"<company>" chief * officer`.
4. Conference speaker bios, podcasts, and the company's engineering blog author pages (good for VPs and Heads).
5. For each department (engineering, product, finance, marketing, sales, operations, legal, people, security, design, data), do one targeted search if you haven't found its head yet.

## Output: `docs/validation/<domain>-scout.md`

```markdown
# Independent coverage scan: <domain>
Run: <ISO timestamp> · Searches: N · Pages fetched: M

## Leaders found
| # | Name | Title (as written) | Seniority | Function | Location (if stated) | Source URL | Source type | Source date | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Confidence: high = company site / SEC filing; medium = reputable news or press release from the last 18 months; low = single older or secondary source.

## Departments with no identified head
## Conflicts (sources disagree on a title or whether someone is current)
## Notes on source availability (blocked pages, JS-only pages, paywalls)
```

Return a 5-line summary to the main agent: the count by seniority, departments with no head found, and the biggest uncertainties. Then, **in the main session** (not by you), the main agent diffs your list against `data/<domain>/leadership.json`:
- People you found that the pipeline missed go into the **Known misses** section of `docs/VALIDATION.md`.
- People the pipeline found that you didn't get flagged for a closer look.
== .claude/agents/source-verifier.md
---
name: source-verifier
description: Independently verifies every collected leadership record against its cited source. Use PROACTIVELY after each collection run (phase 4) and before any human validation pass. Read-only on the dataset; writes only its own report.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, Write
model: sonnet
---

You are a meticulous data-quality auditor. Your job is to decide, record by record, whether the collected leadership data is **actually supported by its cited evidence**. You did not build this pipeline and you owe it nothing. Assume every record could be wrong until the source proves otherwise.

## Inputs

- The domain to audit (e.g. `robinhood.com`). If it isn't given, audit every folder under `data/`.
- `data/<domain>/leadership.json`: people, roles, facts, and sources (with `raw_path` to cached pages).
- Cached raw pages at each source's `raw_path`.

## Hard rules

- **Never modify** anything under `data/`, `src/`, or `docs/VALIDATION.md`. Your only writable file is `docs/validation/<domain>-verifier.md`.
- **Never fetch linkedin.com** or any site whose ToS forbids automated access.
- Judge only from the source text. Don't use your own knowledge of who works where. If you "know" a fact that the source doesn't state, the verdict is still UNSUPPORTED.
- Don't soften verdicts. A wrong record caught now is the point of this agent.

## Procedure (for every person, every fact)

1. **Integrity check (cached copy).** Open the cached raw page. Confirm the `evidence_snippet` appears in it (whitespace- and case-insensitive). If it doesn't, the verdict is `UNSUPPORTED` with reason "snippet not in source". That points to an extraction or hallucination bug.
2. **Semantic check.** Read the surrounding context (about ±500 chars). Does the snippet actually say *this person* holds *this title* at *this company*? Watch for these traps:
   - a former role ("previously CFO at…")
   - a different company (a board seat elsewhere, a prior employer, a partner company)
   - a different person with a similar name
   - an advisor or investor listed as an executive
   - a title that's only implied
3. **Classification check.** Is `function` and `seniority` correct for `title_raw`? For example, "Head of People" is function `people`, seniority `head`. "SVP, Engineering" is seniority `vp`. "Chief of Staff" is not `c_level`.
4. **Freshness check (live).** WebFetch the source URL once. If the page is gone or no longer lists the person, mark the record `STALE` or `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. Spot-check at most 15 live URLs per company, prioritizing C-level records and single-source records.
5. **Duplicate check.** Flag records that look like the same person under name variants (e.g. "Vlad Tenev" / "Vladimir Tenev").

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SUPPORTED` | Snippet present, and it clearly states this person, title, and company as current |
| `PARTIAL` | Person and company are correct, but the title, location, or classification is off |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | Snippet missing, or it doesn't establish the claim |
| `STALE` | Was supported, but the live page no longer shows it |
| `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` | Cache missing and the live fetch failed |

## Output: `docs/validation/<domain>-verifier.md`

```markdown
# Source verification: <domain>
Run: <ISO timestamp> · Records checked: N · Live URLs spot-checked: M

## Summary
SUPPORTED: n · PARTIAL: n · UNSUPPORTED: n · STALE: n · SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: n
Estimated precision (SUPPORTED / total): xx%

## Records
| # | Person | Field | Stored value | Verdict | Reason (1 line) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Suspected duplicates
## Classification corrections (title_raw → suggested function/seniority)
## Pipeline bugs suspected (patterns, not one-offs)
```

Then return a 5-line summary to the main agent: the counts, the worst 3 issues, and any pattern that suggests a pipeline bug. **Make no fixes yourself.** Fixes happen in the main session, after the human reviews your report.

4. **Freshness check (live).** WebFetch the source URL once. If the page is gone or no longer lists the person, mark the record `STALE` or `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. Spot-check at most 15 live URLs per company, prioritizing C-level records and single-source records.
5. **Duplicate check.** Flag records that look like the same person under name variants (e.g. "Vlad Tenev" / "Vladimir Tenev").

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SUPPORTED` | Snippet present, and it clearly states this person, title, and company as current |
| `PARTIAL` | Person and company are correct, but the title, location, or classification is off |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | Snippet missing, or it doesn't establish the claim |
| `STALE` | Was supported, but the live page no longer shows it |
| `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` | Cache missing and the live fetch failed |

## Output: `docs/validation/<domain>-verifier.md`

```markdown
# Source verification: <domain>
Run: <ISO timestamp> · Records checked: N · Live URLs spot-checked: M

## Summary
SUPPORTED: n · PARTIAL: n · UNSUPPORTED: n · STALE: n · SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: n
Estimated precision (SUPPORTED / total): xx%

## Records
| # | Person | Field | Stored value | Verdict | Reason (1 line) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Suspected duplicates
## Classification corrections (title_raw → suggested function/seniority)
## Pipeline bugs suspected (patterns, not one-offs)
```

Then return a 5-line summary to the main agent: the counts, the worst 3 issues, and any pattern that suggests a pipeline bug. **Make no fixes yourself.** Fixes happen in the main session, after the human reviews your report.

"""Builds docs/VALIDATION.md from the committed data and the subagent reports (no LLM).

Per company: every stored person with their best evidence, the pipeline's own review lists,
the source-verifier's verdict ("Agent verdict"), and an empty "Verified by Daniel" column
for the hand-check. Hand-written sections (Known misses, notes) live in
docs/validation/<domain>-notes.md and are included verbatim, so regenerating never
overwrites them. Daniel's ticks go in that column after the last regeneration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from leadership.config import REPO_ROOT

DOCS = REPO_ROOT / "docs"
VERDICT_RANK = {"UNSUPPORTED": 0, "PARTIAL": 1, "STALE": 2, "SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE": 3, "SUPPORTED": 4}
DANIEL = "✅ / ❌ / note"

REVIEW_TITLES = {
    "seat_conflicts": "Seat conflicts (two current holders of one C-suite seat; not decided)",
    "conflicts": "Conflicts between sources",
    "possible_duplicates": "Possible duplicates (not merged)",
    "merged_by_nickname_rule": "Merged by the nickname rule (D6)",
    "from_blocked_host": "From a bot-blocked company host: check in your browser (D13)",
    "reanchored": "Evidence re-anchored from the source text (D22)",
    "stale_single_source": "Single source older than 18 months (low confidence)",
    "c_level_not_in_proxy_undated": "C-level title not in the latest proxy, source undated",
    "superseded_by_proxy": "Retired by the proxy rule (D16)",
    "superseded_by_promotion": "Superseded by a later title",
    "founder_historical": "Founders without a current operating role (D23)",
}


def _cell(text: Any, limit: int = 160) -> str:
    s = " ".join(str(text if text is not None else "").split()).replace("|", "\\|")
    return s if len(s) <= limit else s[: limit - 1] + "…"


def parse_verifier(path: Path) -> dict[str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]:

    )
    out += ["", f"### Current leadership ({len(current)})", ""]
    out.append(
        "| # | Name | Current role(s) | Seniority / function | Confidence | Sources | "
        "Evidence (best) | Review flags | Agent verdict | Verified by Daniel |"
    )
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for i, p in enumerate(current, 1):
        roles = [r for r in p["roles"] if r["is_current"]]
        fact = _best_title_fact(p)
        evidence = f"\"{_cell(fact['evidence_snippet'], 140)}\" [source]({fact['source']['url']})" if fact else ""
        out.append(
            f"| {i} | {_cell(p['full_name'])} | {_cell('; '.join(r['title_raw'] for r in roles))} | "
            f"{_cell('; '.join(r['seniority'] + '/' + r['function'] for r in roles))} | "
            f"{p['confidence']} | {p['source_count']} | {evidence} | "
            f"{_cell(', '.join(_flags(p['full_name'], review)))} | "
            f"{_cell(_agent_verdict(verdicts.get(p['full_name'])), 220)} | {DANIEL} |"
        )
    out += ["", f"### Not current (kept for history) ({len(former)})", ""]
    out.append("| # | Name | Role(s) | Why not current | As of | Agent verdict | Verified by Daniel |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for i, p in enumerate(former, 1):
        out.append(
            f"| {i} | {_cell(p['full_name'])} | {_cell('; '.join(r['title_raw'] for r in p['roles']))} | "
            f"{_cell('; '.join(sorted({r['note'] or 'former' for r in p['roles']})))} | "
            f"{_cell(max((r['as_of'] or '' for r in p['roles']), default='') or 'undated')} | "
            f"{_cell(_agent_verdict(verdicts.get(p['full_name'])), 220)} | {DANIEL} |"
        )

    out += ["", "### Review lists from the pipeline", ""]
    for key, title in REVIEW_TITLES.items():
        entries = review.get(key)
        if not entries:
            continue
        out += [f"**{title}** ({len(entries)})", ""]
        for e in entries:
            out.append(f"- {_cell(_describe(key, e), 400)}")
        out.append("")

    stored = {p["full_name"] for p in people}
    rejected: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in stats.get("rejections", []):
        rejected.setdefault(r["full_name"], []).append(r)
    dropped = {n: rs for n, rs in rejected.items() if n not in stored and not _merged(n, stored)}
    out += [f"### People with every claim rejected ({len(dropped)})", ""]
    out.append("| Name | Titles claimed | Reason(s) | Example source | Verified by Daniel |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for n, rs in sorted(dropped.items()):
        out.append(
            f"| {_cell(n)} | {_cell('; '.join(sorted({r['title'] for r in rs})))} | "
            f"{_cell('; '.join(sorted({r['reason'] for r in rs})))} | [{len(rs)} claim(s)]"
            f"({rs[0]['url']}) | {DANIEL} |"
        )
    notes = DOCS / "validation" / f"{domain}-notes.md"
    if notes.exists():
        out += ["", notes.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _merged(name: str, stored: set[str]) -> bool:
    from leadership.models import normalize_name

    key = normalize_name(name)
    toks = key.split()
    return any(
        normalize_name(s) == key or (toks and normalize_name(s).split()[-1:] == toks[-1:])
        for s in stored
    )


def _describe(key: str, e: dict) -> str:
    if key == "seat_conflicts":
        holders = "; ".join(f"{h['person']} ({h['title']}, as of {h['as_of'] or 'undated'})" for h in e["holders"])
        return f"{e.get('seat')}: {holders}"
    if "names" in e:
        return " / ".join(e["names"])
    parts = [e.get("person", ""), e.get("title", ""), e.get("field", "")]
    if "values" in e:
        parts.append(" vs ".join(e["values"]))
    if e.get("note"):
        parts.append(e["note"])
    if "evidence_snippet" in e:
        parts.append(f"\"{e['evidence_snippet']}\"")
    if "only_source" in e:
        parts.append("only source" if e["only_source"] else "also has other sources")
    urls = e.get("urls") or ([e["url"]] if e.get("url") else [])
    parts.append(" ".join(urls[:3]) + (f" (+{len(urls) - 3} more)" if len(urls) > 3 else ""))
    return " · ".join(p for p in parts if p)

Generated by `leadership validation-report` from `data/<domain>/leadership.json` and the
subagent reports in `docs/validation/`. **Agent verdict** is the source-verifier's verdict
on that person's facts, an input, not an approval. **Verified by Daniel** is for the
hand-check: ✅ correct, ❌ wrong, or a note.

How to hand-check: open the evidence link, find the quoted snippet, and confirm the person,
the title, and that it is current. Records from investors.robinhood.com must be checked in a
browser (the host blocks automated clients; D13).
"""

    text = HEADER + "".join("\n" + company_section(d) for d in domains)
    path = DOCS / "VALIDATION.md"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return path
